fulltext_screening_results.reason: This is a task-based fMRI study that explicitly instructed cognitive reappraisal (reappraise vs attend). Emotional stimuli were visual (IAPS and validated alcohol images). The sample includes alcohol-dependent patients and matched healthy controls with results reported separately. The paper reports within-task contrasts (reappraise > attend per emotion; attend emotion > attend neutral) and whole-brain second-level voxelwise analyses with standard-space coordinates and corrected thresholds. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply.

The full text meets all required inclusion criteria: it is a task-based fMRI study that uses instructed emotion regulation (cognitive reappraisal: downregulate and upregulate) with visual stimuli (IAPS pictures). The sample (healthy participants; genotype groups reported) is acceptable, and the paper reports within-task contrasts relevant to regulation (downregulate > look, upregulate > look, negative > neutral). Group-level whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses are reported with peak coordinates and cluster thresholds in standard space, satisfying whole-brain evidence. The manuscript includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-empirical, or empathy-without-regulation) are met.

Although this study uses task-based fMRI (NF and backward-masking/emotional conflict tasks) and reports whole-brain group-level results with peak coordinates, it does not meet the review's core requirement that participants be instructed to regulate an emotional response to visual stimuli (I6). The fMRI tasks primarily involve neurofeedback-driven downregulation of amygdala activity (NF vs rest), i.e., volitional modulation of a neural signal, rather than an instructed emotion regulation strategy applied to concurrently presented visual emotional stimuli (e.g., reappraisal of pictures). While visual stimulus tasks (backward masking; emotional conflict Stroop) are present, regulation was not instructed during those stimulus presentations. Therefore I6 is not satisfied; additionally, the within-task contrasts involving regulation do not specifically reflect instructed emotion regulation of visual stimuli as required (I9 is not met for the meta-analysis target). Full text appears complete. Inclusion criteria met: I5, I7, I8, I10, I11. Inclusion criteria not met: I6, I9. Exclusion criteria met: none.

Full text is complete. Excluded because the study does not instruct participants to regulate their emotional responses (no reappraisal/acceptance/distancing instruction) and thus does not meet the emotion-regulation task requirement. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI) and I8 (sample qualifies). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no instructed emotion-regulation strategy), I7 (regulated stimuli are written statements/sentences rather than the visual image/video stimuli specified), I9 (no within-task contrast of regulation vs. view; contrasts are illness vs. control evaluations, not regulation contrasts), and I10 (no clearly reported whole-brain, group-level task activation map surviving whole-brain correction; reported results rely on small-volume/ROI corrections). Exclusion criterion met: E4 (results are reported with small-volume corrections/ROIs rather than whole-brain-corrected findings). Therefore the study does not satisfy the review’s core inclusion requirements and must be excluded.

This is a task-based fMRI study (I5) using visual negative pictures (I7) in a healthy sample (I8) and it reports within-task contrasts comparing inhibition-priming versus neutral-priming (I9). However, the study did not instruct participants to use any explicit emotion-regulation strategy; it used word-priming to induce automatic (implicit) regulation rather than an instructed regulation task, so it does not meet I6. Moreover, the reported neuroimaging results are presented via an ROI-focused analysis (exploratory ROI percent-signal-change and ROI-based contrasts) with no accompanying whole-brain voxelwise group-level activation tables or peak coordinates described, which fails I10 and corresponds to exclusion criterion E4 (ONLY ROI/ small-volume results with no whole-brain analysis). Full text appears complete. Therefore the study is excluded.

The study is a task-based fMRI investigation of instructed emotion regulation (cognitive reappraisal) using visual stimuli (IAPS images) in patients with MDD and matched controls, with within-task contrasts (negative decrease > negative look) and whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses reported (including Talairach coordinates and cluster-thresholded maps). The full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not non-empirical, and it reports within-task effects). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and should be included.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs participants to perform cognitive reappraisal (downregulate/upregulate/maintain) while viewing visual emotional stimuli (IAPS images). The manuscript reports within-task contrasts of interest (downregulate > maintain, upregulate > maintain, negative > neutral) and presents group-level whole-brain analyses and ROI analyses, with statistical maps available on Neurovault. The sample includes younger and older adults and the analyses meet the meta-analysis requirements. Although some participants had incomplete brain coverage, whole-brain group-level results were nevertheless performed and reported. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs cognitive reappraisal to down-regulate emotion (explicit ‘decrease’ vs ‘look’ instructions), uses visual stimuli (IAPS pictures), reports within-task regulation and reactivity contrasts (decrease negative > look negative; look negative > look neutral), and presents group-level whole-brain analyses with peak coordinates/tables. Methods, results and discussion are fully reported. No exclusion criteria are met (no ROI-only, no connectivity-only, not non-empirical). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs participants to regulate emotion (diminish/enhance/maintain) using cognitive reappraisal-like strategies during presentation of visual stimuli (IAPS images). It reports within-task contrasts (diminish>maintain, enhance>maintain, maintain>diminish) and presents group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses with peak coordinates and thresholding. The sample includes clinical (PTSD, trauma-exposed non-PTSD) and healthy control groups with separate reporting. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (I5–I11) and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs participants to use cognitive reappraisal (up- and down-regulation) during an fMRI Ultimatum Game and during IAPS training, fulfilling the review focus on instructed emotion regulation. Stimuli are visual (IAPS pictures in training and photographs of proposers/faces during the task). The manuscript reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (e.g., Down > Look, Down < Look < Up, regulated decisions contrasts) and whole-brain group-level voxelwise analyses with peak coordinates and cluster-level FWE correction. Participant sample is healthy adults and methods/results/discussion are fully presented. No exclusion criteria (ROIs-only, connectivity-only, non-empirical, or perspective-taking without regulation) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I5–I11) and should be included.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs participants to use emotion regulation strategies (cognitive reappraisal and expressive suppression) while viewing visual emotional stimuli (film clips). The paper reports within-task contrasts (reappraise > watch-negative; suppress > watch-negative; watch-negative > watch-neutral) and presents group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses with reported peak coordinates and tables. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI experiment that explicitly instructs an emotion regulation strategy (cognitive reappraisal) and also includes a placebo regulation condition. Visual emotional stimuli (IAPS pictures) were used. The sample comprises healthy adult participants. The paper reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (e.g. RU–CUR, PU–CUP and related conjunction/subtraction contrasts) and presents group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses with peak coordinates and tables/figures in standard space. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only reporting, connectivity-only analyses, non-empirical paper, or empathy-only perspective tasks) are met. Therefore the study meets all listed inclusion criteria and should be included in the meta-analysis.

The full text meets all inclusion requirements for the review: it is a task-based fMRI study (I5) that instructs an emotion regulation strategy (cognitive reappraisal; Suppress condition) during stimulus presentation (I6). Stimuli are visual (IAPS static images; I7). The sample is healthy adult participants (I8). The analyses report within-task regulation contrasts (e.g., Suppress > Maintain, Maintain > Suppress) and parametric covariates of subjective ratings (I9). Group-level, whole-brain random-effects SPM analyses with peak coordinates in standard space are reported (I10,I11). The full article contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion (fulltext_complete). No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-empirical, or empathy-without-regulation issues). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This paper reports a task-based fMRI study in which participants were explicitly instructed to use cognitive reappraisal to down-regulate negative affect elicited by visual stimuli (IAPS pictures). The methods describe block-wise Reappraise and Maintain conditions, online self-report ratings, and within-task contrasts including conjunctions ([Maintain > Baseline] AND [Reappraise > Baseline]) used to identify amygdala activation as well as task-dependent PPI contrasts (Reappraise > Maintain). Group-level, voxelwise analyses are reported with peak coordinates (e.g., left amygdala MNI −22,0,−22) and whole-brain PPI results (Table 1, figures). The study therefore meets inclusion criteria I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (instructed emotion regulation — reappraisal), I7 (visual stimuli), I8 (eligible sample), I9 (within-task contrasts related to regulation), I10 (group-level whole-brain maps with peak coordinates), and I11 (results reported in tables/figures/text). No exclusion criteria are met (not only ROI/only connectivity-only; whole-brain task analyses are present). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study using an instructed antecedent-focused emotion regulation manipulation (precedent descriptions presenting images as fictitious vs real), fulfilling the review’s definition of extrinsic/incidental reappraisal. Stimuli were visual static images (mutilation/IAPS), participants were healthy adults, and the paper reports within-task contrasts (unpleasant > neutral) and ROI paired tests showing attenuation of amygdala/insula responses. Whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed and coordinates/peaks are reported; standard group-level analyses were used. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs emotion regulation strategies (reappraisal and acceptance) during presentation of visual sad images (IAPS and normed photos). The sample includes remitted MDD and control participants with separate group analyses. The paper reports within-task contrasts (accept > reappraise, accept > view, reappraise > view) and whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses with reported cluster results/locations in tables and text. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Although an a priori mask/SVC was noted for some analyses, whole-brain clusters outside frontal/amygdala (e.g., insula) are reported, supporting whole-brain task-evoked results. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructed participants to apply emotion-regulation strategies (mindfulness and a cognitive reappraisal “reality checking”) during the anticipation and perception of emotional pictures. Stimuli were visual IAPS images. The paper reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (e.g., exp ng > nt, per ng > nt), presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with cluster correction and tables/figures of activations, and provides full Methods, Results, and Discussion. Sample is healthy adults. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10 and I11. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply. Full text appears complete.

This study should be excluded because the emotional stimuli being regulated are non-visual (anticipation of somatosensory pain via intraepidermal electrical stimulation), which fails inclusion criterion I7 (stimuli must be VISUAL). The study does meet multiple inclusion criteria: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (instructed cognitive reappraisal during anticipation), I8 (eligible sample: healthy participants reported separately), I9 (reports within-task contrasts related to regulation, e.g., regulation vs. anxiety), I10 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported), and I11 (results/coordinates described). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) are triggered. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore excluded due to not meeting I7 (non-visual regulated stimuli).

This article reports an empirical, task-based fMRI experiment in which participants were explicitly instructed to perform cognitive reappraisal (interpretation/reinterpretation via contextual titles) of visual emotional stimuli (IAPS pictures). The sample (young adult university participants) is eligible. The fMRI analysis includes within-task contrasts related to regulation (IAPS2–IAPS1 for up-/down-regulation) and reports group-level whole-brain activation results with peak coordinates (e.g., left middle temporal gyrus coordinates provided; Table 2 referenced). The full text includes methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not review-only, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group without within-task effects, not an empathy task lacking regulation instructions). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and is suitable for the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs cognitive reappraisal (reappraise vs attend), using visual stimuli (IAPS pictures), with both an at-risk clinical group and healthy controls whose results are reported separately. The analyses include within-task contrasts for regulation (Reappraisal > Attend Negative) and unregulated viewing (View Negative > View Neutral), performed as group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with reported peak MNI coordinates and cluster-level FWE correction. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (not a review, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, reports within-task effects, not purely perspective-taking). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that instructed an emotion regulation strategy (detachment/distancing, a form of cognitive reappraisal) during presentation of visual stimuli (IAPS/EmoPicS images). It reports within-task contrasts comparing regulation and permit conditions (e.g., Negative Detach vs. Negative Permit) and conducts second-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with reported peak coordinates in standard (MNI) space; ROI analyses are supplementary. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (e.g., only ROI results, connectivity-only, non-empirical) apply. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria I5–I11 and should be included.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs cognitive reappraisal (reappraise > look contrasts) and reports within-task contrasts. Stimuli include visual faces (fearful and neutral) used during the instruction/regulation period; although top-down generation used sentences as background, the regulated stimulus during instruction is a visual face, so the study meets the visual-stimuli requirement. The sample (healthy adult women) is acceptable. The paper reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses and tables/figures of activations and coordinates. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it satisfies I5–I11 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This full-text reports a task-based BOLD fMRI study that instructed participants to use cognitive reappraisal ("Reduce Emotion") vs maintain responses to negative images (I5, I6). Stimuli were visual IAPS pictures (I7). Participant groups include healthy controls and clinical groups with results reported separately (I8). The paper reports within-task contrasts (Reappraise vs Baseline; Maintain vs Baseline; and task effects/interaction) and behavioral-fMRI relationships (I9). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are presented with cluster thresholds and peak coordinates in Talairach space (I10), and results are reported in tables/figures/supplement (I11). No exclusion criteria are met (not a review; reports whole-brain task activation maps; not only connectivity or ROI-only; includes within-group task effects; not an empathy/perspective-taking study). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and is eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs participants to use causal attributions as an emotion-regulation strategy while viewing visual stimuli (static facial images). The paper reports within-task contrasts (internal>view, external>view, emotion-specific contrasts) and whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses with cluster-level correction and reported coordinates/tables. Participant groups (MDD and matched healthy controls) are reported separately. The full text includes Introduction, Methods (task, imaging, preprocessing, statistics), Results (behavioral, fMRI, connectivity) and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria apply (not a review, not ROI-only, includes task activation maps, includes within-group effects, and the instructed task explicitly directs emotion regulation rather than mere perspective-taking). All relevant inclusion criteria I5–I11 are satisfied.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study that explicitly used a cognitive reappraisal (emotion regulation) paradigm with instructed regulation (Suppress/reappraise) and a passive Observe condition. Emotional stimuli were visual IAPS pictures. The paper reports within-task contrasts of interest (Maintain>Observe and Suppress>Maintain) and describes group-level whole-brain voxel-wise analyses with correction and supplementary tables for full results/coordinates. The sample includes cocaine-dependent groups and a healthy control group with group results reported separately. No exclusion criteria are met (e.g., not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not non-empirical). The full text includes introduction, methods, results and discussion; supplementary tables are referenced but their absence does not render the main text incomplete.

This study is a task-based fMRI investigation that instructs cognitive reappraisal (distancing) during presentation of visual emotional stimuli (IAPS images). It reports within-task contrasts (Reappraise > Experience; Experience > Reappraise), uses whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses with reported peak coordinates and whole-brain correction, and provides full methods, results, and discussion in the full text. All required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

This article meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis: it is an empirical, task-based fMRI study (I5) that instructs an emotion-regulation strategy (cognitive reappraisal: “decrease negative”) during presentation of stimuli (I6). Stimuli were visual static images (negative and neutral pictures) (I7). The sample includes clinical (female adolescents with conduct disorder) and typically developing control groups reported separately (I8). Analyses report within-task contrasts relevant to regulation (decrease negative > look negative) and unregulated viewing contrasts (look negative > look neutral) (I9). Group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses were conducted and whole-brain familywise-error-corrected results are reported (cluster-level FWE and references to peak/cluster reports), satisfying the whole-brain reporting requirement (I10,I11). No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, no connectivity-only, within-group effects are reported). Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs cognitive reappraisal (Increase/Decrease) during presentation of visual emotional stimuli (static angry face photographs). The paper reports within-task contrasts (e.g., Decrease > Observe-angry, Increase > Observe-angry), whole-brain group-level voxelwise analyses with peak coordinates and tables, and provides full methods, results, and discussion. Sample is healthy adults and resting-state subset is reported but task analyses meet meta-analysis objectives. Full text appears complete.

This study is a task-based fMRI investigation that instructs cognitive reappraisal (Reappraise-Neg vs Maintain-Neg), uses visual stimuli (static facial images), reports within-task contrasts relevant to emotion regulation, and provides group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with reported activations/coordinates. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply.

This full text reports an original, task-based fMRI experiment in which participants were explicitly instructed to use cognitive reappraisal (Increase/Decrease) while viewing visual emotional stimuli (IAPS images). It includes behavioral and physiological validation, within-task contrasts (e.g. Increase > Look-Negative; Decrease > Look-Negative), and group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with reported thresholds/coordinates. The methods, results, and discussion are complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study of instructed emotion regulation (cognitive reappraisal via distancing) in youth using visual stimuli (validated photographs), meeting the review’s core design. The paper reports within-task contrasts focused on regulation (Far) versus baseline and Far versus Look-Negative, and describes traditional univariate (GLM) whole-brain analyses with data registered to MNI152 and univariate results provided in the Supplement, satisfying the requirement for group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps/coordinates. The sample (typically developing children/adolescents) is eligible. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only results, connectivity-only analyses, non-empirical work) apply. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; supplementary univariate results are referenced. Thus all inclusion criteria I5–I11 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study that explicitly instructs cognitive reappraisal (emotion regulation) of visual stimuli (IAPS pictures). It reports within-task contrasts relevant to regulation (Reappraise Negative > Attend Negative) and an unregulated viewing contrast (Attend Negative > Attend Neutral). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported with peak coordinates and FWE cluster correction. Sample (n=62 young adults) is eligible. Although resting-state analyses are also included, the paper clearly contains task activation results, so no exclusion criteria are met. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided and appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study (I5) using visual IAPS pictures (I7). The task explicitly instructs an emotion-regulation strategy (voluntary attentional regulation: shape-evaluation vs valence-evaluation), meeting the instructed regulation criterion (I6). The sample includes MDD patients and healthy controls with results reported separately (I8). The paper reports within-task contrasts tied to regulation (SRT vs ERT and valence contrasts) (I9). Analyses are whole-brain, voxelwise group-level SPM second-level tests with voxelwise and cluster-FWE thresholds and extraction of local activation peaks (I10); results/coordinates are described and supplemental tables are referenced (I11). No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, no connectivity-only, not non-empirical, and within-group effects are reported). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructed participants to use cognitive reappraisal to down-regulate negative emotion (Reduce vs Maintain) while viewing visual stimuli (IAPS images). The paper reports within-task contrasts (Reduce > Maintain and related effects), presents whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses with cluster-correction (AlphaSim) and tables/figures of significant clusters, and includes an eligible sample (anxious and control groups). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion (appears complete). No exclusion criteria apply (not a review; not ROI-only; not connectivity-only; within-task effects are reported; not an empathy/perspective task without regulation). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis: it is a task-based fMRI experiment (I5) using an instructed emotion-regulation paradigm (cognitive reappraisal; I6) with visual stimuli (static IAPS pictures; I7). The sample includes unmedicated panic-disorder patients and healthy controls with results reported (I8). The paper reports within-task contrasts relevant to regulation (e.g., Reappraise vs Maintain, Maintain vs Reappraise; I9). Group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported with standard-space coordinates and Z-values (MNI peaks cited; I10/I11). The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met. The task uses a competitive reaction-time paradigm with social provocation and auditory white-noise punishments; regulation instructions (reappraisal) target responses to provocation/auditory events rather than regulation of an emotional response to visual stimuli. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (instructed cognitive reappraisal strategy), I8 (sample acceptable), I9 (reports within-task contrasts such as win>lose and lose>win), I10 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported), and I11 (whole-brain results described/tabled). Inclusion criteria not met: I7 (emotional stimuli are not visual). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) are triggered. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based (event-related) fMRI study that explicitly instructed emotion-regulation strategies (reappraisal and expressive suppression) during an anticipation (cue) and stimulus (target) period. Visual stimuli were used (IAPS negative images). The paper reports within-task contrasts (e.g., Target Reappraisal > Target Appraise, Cue Suppression > Cue Reappraisal) and presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with FWE correction and MNI coordinates in tables. The full text includes methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I11 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs cognitive reappraisal (I5, I6). Stimuli were visual IAPS pictures (static images) (I7). The sample includes clinical groups (BD, SZ) and healthy controls with results reported separately (I8). The analyses include within-task contrasts related to regulation (reappraise > attend-negative; attend-negative > attend-neutral) (I9). Whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses were performed (3dMVM in AFNI) with cluster correction and reported cluster results (I10, I11). No exclusion criteria are met: the study is empirical with original fMRI data (not E3), reports whole-brain results (not only ROI; not E4), is not only connectivity/resting-state (not E5), includes within-task effects (not E6), and is not an empathy/perspective task without regulation instruction (not E7). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria.

Exclusion rationale: No instructed emotion regulation during the fMRI task (participants completed a dispositional reappraisal questionnaire but were not instructed to reappraise), therefore inclusion criterion I6 is not met. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli: aversive and neutral images), I8 (eligible sample), I9 (reports within-task unregulated contrast: aversive > neutral anticipation), I10 (reports whole-brain exploratory analysis with peak coordinates), I11 (whole-brain results clearly described). Exclusion criteria met: none. Because ALL inclusion criteria must be satisfied and I6 is not satisfied, the study is excluded.

This full-text meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis. It is a task-based fMRI study (I5) that explicitly instructs emotion regulation strategies including cognitive reappraisal and expressive suppression (I6). Emotional stimuli were visual static images from the IAPS (I7). The sample includes a clinical group (schizophrenia) and healthy controls, with task results reported for patient group (I8). The analyses report within-task contrasts relevant to regulation (reappraise > attend negative; suppress > attend negative) (I9). Whole-brain random-effects analyses were performed and reported (cluster-level FWE correction), with results presented in text/figures/tables consistent with standard MNI coordinates (I10,I11). No exclusion criteria apply: the paper reports whole-brain task activation maps (not only ROI or connectivity-only results). Full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore include in the meta-analysis.

Although this is a task-based, whole-brain fMRI study using visual stimuli (IAPS) with within-task contrasts (EXP neg > neut, PRES neg > neut) and reports peak coordinates (meeting I5, I7, I8, I9, I10, I11), it does NOT instruct participants to implement an emotion-regulation strategy during scanning. The study selects participants on habitual use of reappraisal vs. suppression (ERQ) and examines correlations with activation, but there is no instructed regulation condition (failure to meet I6). No exclusion criteria are triggered. Therefore it must be excluded because it does not satisfy inclusion criterion I6 (fMRI task with instructed emotion regulation).

This is a task-based fMRI study that explicitly instructs emotion regulation (diminish/enhance/maintain) using a cognitive reappraisal-like strategy (imagining less/more negative outcomes). Stimuli are visual (IAPS pictures, including trauma-related images). The sample includes PTSD patients and matched healthy controls with results reported for groups. The analysis includes within-task contrasts (negative-diminish, negative-enhance, negative-maintain) and group-level, whole-brain voxelwise random-effects analyses with cluster correction (AlphaSim), and significant clusters/activations are reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not non-empirical, and includes within-task effects). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study that explicitly instructs participants in two regulation-related conditions (attention shifting: indoor/outdoor; appraisal/labeling: like/dislike) in addition to an implicit viewing condition. Stimuli are visual static composite images (faces/scenes). Participants are healthy adults. The paper reports within-task contrasts relevant to regulation (male/female–face-only; indoor/outdoor–male/female; like/dislike–male/female) and provides group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with peak coordinates (MNI) and FWE correction. Full article includes methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (I5–I11) and violates no exclusion criteria.

The full text reports an original, task-based fMRI experiment using an instructed emotion regulation strategy (cognitive reappraisal) with visual stimuli (IAPS pictures). Participants include clinical (PTSD) and combat-exposed control groups with group-level analyses reported separately. The paper reports within-task contrasts relevant to regulation (Reappraise > Maintain) and unregulated viewing contrasts (Maintain > Look), and provides whole-brain voxelwise results with peak coordinates and corrected thresholds. The manuscript includes complete methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10, and I11. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete.

All required elements for inclusion are present. This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study using instructed cognitive reappraisal (increase/decrease/maintain) with visual stimuli (IAPS images). It reports within-task contrasts relevant to regulation (increase > maintain; decrease > maintain) and an unregulated viewing contrast (negative > neutral). Group-level whole-brain random-effects analyses are reported with peak coordinates in MNI space in tables and figures. The full text contains background, methods, results, and discussion (complete core content). No exclusion criteria apply. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10, and I11, and no exclusion criteria (E3–E7) are met.

This is a task-based fMRI study that presents visual emotional stimuli (IAPS pictures) and reports within-task contrasts (negative > neutral) as well as group-level whole-brain activation results. Participants include a clinical group (BPD) and healthy controls analyzed separately. Although the task did not instruct an emotion regulation strategy, the review accepts unregulated viewing contrasts (I9); therefore the study still meets the meta-analysis objective. The paper provides whole-brain voxelwise analyses (cluster-level results with FDR correction) and ROI follow-ups, and reports sufficient methodological details and results for inclusion.

Study 2 reports a task-based fMRI experiment using instructed cognitive reappraisal ("CHANGE" vs "LOOK") during presentation of visual IAPS images. The paper reports within-task contrasts (look negative > look neutral; decrease negative > look negative) and group-level whole-brain analyses with peak coordinates reported (Table 5). Participant groups (DSH and depression control) are reported separately. Full text includes methods, results, and discussion. Thus all required inclusion criteria (I5–I11) are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs cognitive emotion regulation (reappraisal: enhance/suppress/maintain) using visual IAPS pictures, with a sample of healthy participants. The paper reports within-task contrasts (e.g., suppress > maintain, enhance > maintain) and uses whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (data normalized to Talairach space; cluster-size thresholding reported) including voxelwise PPI connectivity maps. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10, and I11 and does not meet any exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study in which children (8–12 yrs) were instructed to use a cognitive reappraisal strategy (“MAKE-POSITIVE”) while viewing visual sad images (IAPS and child-appropriate photos). The paper reports within-task contrasts (reappraise sad vs. view sad; view sad vs. view neutral) and conducts group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (with corrected thresholds) as well as ROI analyses. Core article sections (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion) are present. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the review (I5–I11). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs cognitive reappraisal (self-focused increase and decrease) during presentation of visual stimuli (anger facial photographs). The paper reports behavioral and neural within-task contrasts (e.g., increase > view-angry, decrease > view-angry, view-angry > view-neutral), provides whole-brain group-level results with anatomical localization and tables/figures in standard space, and reports patient and healthy control groups separately. The full text includes Introduction, Methods (participants, task, fMRI acquisition and analysis), Results, and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria apply. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the review and is appropriate for meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study that explicitly instructs cognitive reappraisal (Decrease) during presentation of visual stimuli (IAPS images), meeting the review objective. The paper reports within-task regulation contrasts (e.g. Negative Decrease vs Negative Look; Neutral Decrease vs Neutral Look) and presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with MNI peak coordinates and cluster-based correction. Both bipolar patients and healthy controls are included and reported separately. The full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, or non-empirical paper). Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I11 are satisfied and the study should be included.

This full text meets all inclusion criteria: it is a task-based fMRI study (I5) that instructs cognitive reappraisal (reduce vs. maintain) as the emotion-regulation strategy (I6); stimuli are visual static pictures from the Native Chinese Affective Picture System (I7); participants are healthy adult volunteers (I8); the paper reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (reduce vs. maintain) (I9); analyses include group-level whole-brain voxelwise tests with reported peak coordinates and FDR correction (I10), and results/coordinates are clearly described in the text (I11). No exclusion criteria apply (e.g., not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not non-empirical). The provided full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion (appears complete).

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the review: it is a task-based fMRI experiment (I5) that instructs cognitive reappraisal as the regulation strategy (I6); stimuli are visual IAPS pictures presented during the task (I7); sample comprises healthy adult participants (I8); the paper reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (e.g. RU–CU, CU–CN) (I9); a group-level whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analysis is reported with peak coordinates and threshold (P<0.001) (I10); results are described in text and figures (I11). No exclusion criteria are met: this is empirical original fMRI activation work with whole-brain analyses (not ROI-only, connectivity-only, or non-empirical). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a task-based fMRI study that explicitly instructed cognitive reappraisal (Increase and Decrease) during presentation of visual emotional stimuli (film clips), satisfying the intervention/strategy requirement. Stimuli were visual (first-person extreme sports film clips). The sample (healthy adult participants) is eligible. The paper reports within-task contrasts related to emotion regulation (e.g., Increase + Decrease vs Look-Sports) and provides group-level whole-brain random-effects analyses with tables/figures of peak coordinates. Although DCM/effective connectivity analyses are included, whole-brain activation results are also reported. No exclusion criteria apply (not a review; not ROI-only; not connectivity-only; includes within-group task effects; not an empathy-only task). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study of instructed emotion regulation using cognitive reappraisal (decrease vs look contrasts) with visual stimuli (IAPS images). The sample includes adolescents (clinical subgroup with suicidal ideation and controls). The paper reports within-task contrasts (decrease > look; look negative > look neutral) and whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses with reported cluster peaks. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, enabling assessment. All inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

(a) Exclusion IDs met: none. (b) Inclusion IDs met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (instructed emotion regulation: distancing reappraisal), I8 (sample acceptable), I9 (within-task reappraisal contrasts reported, e.g., R–NR), I10 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with reported MNI peak coordinates), I11 (results reported in text/tables/figures). (c) Inclusion IDs not met: I7 (emotional stimuli are VISUAL) — NOT MET: the regulated stimuli are anticipatory threat of shock (pain expectation) signaled auditorily; there are no visual emotional stimuli such as images or videos. Because the meta-analysis requires regulation of visual emotional stimuli, this study does not meet criterion I7 and must be excluded.

The full text reports an empirical task-based fMRI study in which participants were instructed to regulate emotion using a distancing (cognitive reappraisal) strategy while viewing visually presented negative and neutral images (I5, I6, I7). The sample includes a clinical group (PMDD) and healthy controls with results reported separately (I8). The paper reports within-task regulation-related contrasts (negative, far > negative, close) and unregulated viewing contrasts (negative > neutral) (I9). It also presents whole-brain, voxel-wise group analyses with peak coordinates in standard (MNI) space and cluster-corrected results (I10,I11). The full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria apply. Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria for the review and is included.

Excluded because stimuli are non-visual autobiographical memory recall (script-driven imagery), so the study does not meet inclusion criterion I7 (visual emotional stimuli). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (instructed emotion regulation; cognitive reappraisal-like “analyze” strategy), I8 (sample eligible), I9 (reports within-task regulation contrasts), I10 (reports whole-brain voxelwise analyses with standard-space coordinates), I11 (results reported in text/tables). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) are triggered by the full text. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study using a fear conditioning/extinction paradigm with visual stimuli and whole-brain voxelwise analyses. However, participants were not instructed to employ an emotion-regulation strategy (e.g., reappraisal, distancing); the task probes unregulated conditioned fear and extinction. Therefore inclusion criterion I6 (instructed emotion regulation task) is not met, so the study does not match the meta-analysis requirement. Full text is complete. Inclusion criteria met: I5, I7, I8, I9, I10, I11. Inclusion criterion not met: I6. No exclusion criteria from the review were triggered.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructed participants to use cognitive reappraisal (reappraise > attend contrast) while viewing visual IAPS images. The paper reports within-task contrasts (Reappraise Negative > Attend Negative; View Negative > View Neutral) and whole-brain group-level analyses with tables of activation peaks and ROI analyses. The sample (high-risk and control young women) is acceptable. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This full text meets all inclusion criteria for the review. It is a task-based fMRI study (I5) using an instructed emotion regulation paradigm with cognitive reappraisal instructions (‘reappraise…so it elicits less negative affect’) (I6). Emotional stimuli are visual pictures (fear and OCD-related images) (I7). The sample includes OCD patients and demographically matched healthy controls with results reported for groups (I8). The paper reports within-task regulation contrasts (fear regulate > attend; OCD-related regulate > attend) (I9). Group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses are performed and peak coordinates are reported in MNI space (figures/tables/text) (I10,I11). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) are met. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion, and references).

The full text reports a task-based fMRI study using instructed affect-labeling (an implicit emotion-regulation manipulation) and an affect-matching (unregulated viewing) task with visual stimuli (photographs of emotional faces). It reports within-task contrasts relevant to regulation (affect label > gender label) and viewing (affect match > shape match). Participants include clinical (SP subgroups) and healthy control groups with group-level SPM analyses normalized to standard space; peak coordinates and whole-brain main effects are reported (supplementary table). The methods, results, and discussion are present and complete. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only reporting, connectivity-only analyses, or non-empirical paper) apply. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis objective.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs cognitive reappraisal (Reduce vs Maintain) of visual images in adolescents, includes a control group reported separately, reports the within-task contrast (Pre-Reduce vs Pre-Maintain; Reduce>Maintain as reappraisal success), and presents whole-brain voxelwise group-level analyses (voxelwise ANCOVA, cluster thresholds and reported clusters/coordinates). The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs cognitive reappraisal while participants view visual images. The paper reports within-task contrasts (reappraise > look), whole-brain group-level voxelwise analyses with thresholding and tables/figures of activations, and provides full methods, results and discussion. Thus it satisfies all inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs an emotion regulation strategy (appraisal condition) using visual stimuli (faces and scenes). The manuscript reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (appraisal vs. implicit emotion processing), and group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with peak coordinates in standard space. The sample (healthy adult males) is eligible. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and no exclusion criteria are met. Therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10,I11) and violates none.

This study fails inclusion criterion I7. Although it is a task-based fMRI RCT (I5) with an instructed emotion-regulation strategy (observe/attention regulation; I6), includes a clinical SAD sample (I8), reports within-task regulation contrasts (regulate vs react; I9), and provides group-level whole-brain voxelwise results with peak coordinates (I10) and coordinate tables described in text (I11), the regulated stimuli are participant-generated autobiographical descriptions and negative self-belief sentences presented as written words/sentences on the screen. The review’s eligibility rules explicitly exclude studies whose regulated stimuli are word/sentence stimuli. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) are otherwise met. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore exclude due to not meeting I7.

This paper reports a task-based fMRI study (Study 2) using an instructed cognitive reappraisal task (regulate vs experience vs observe) with visual stimuli (IAPS pictures). It includes adults from a clinical (gambling disorder patients) and healthy control groups and provides within-task contrasts (‘regulate’ > ‘experience’, ‘experience’ > ‘observe’) and within-group activation maps. Group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported with peak MNI coordinates (e.g. x = -60, y = 20, Z = 32) and cluster thresholds, meeting whole-brain reporting criteria. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the article appears complete. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5–I11 and violates no exclusion criteria.

Full text is complete. Met inclusion: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli: facial images), I8 (eligible sample: healthy adults), I10 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with MNI coordinates), I11 (results reported clearly in text/tables). Not met: I6 — the task did NOT instruct participants to use an emotion regulation strategy (e.g., reappraise, down-regulate, accept). Instead, the Cued Emotional Conflict Task required cognitive control/response mapping (respond to actual vs. opposite emotion) and the study correlated habitual ERQ scores with task activation; participants were not instructed to regulate their emotional responses in-scanner. I9 — there is no within-task contrast that reflects an instructed emotion-regulation condition (e.g., “reappraise > look”, “down-regulate > maintain”) nor a standard unregulated viewing contrast of emotion versus baseline that maps onto passive viewing; the reported contrasts index cognitive control/conflict (opposite vs actual) rather than an explicit regulation instruction. Therefore the study does not satisfy the core requirement (I6) and is excluded.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs an emotion regulation strategy (reality check / cognitive reappraisal) during presentation of visual emotional stimuli (IAPS pictures; also video transfer task). The sample (healthy adults) is eligible. The paper reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (e.g., regulate > view, regulate > baseline) and presents group-level whole-brain analyses (voxel-wise thresholds, cluster corrections) with reported clusters/coordinates. Full text includes introduction, methods, results and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I11 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply.

This study is a task-based fMRI experiment that instructs cognitive reappraisal of visual (IAPS) images and reports within-task contrasts and behavioral validation; however, the full text reports primarily ROI and seed-based (gPPI) connectivity analyses (L amygdala seed → R IFG) and does not present a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked activation map (peak coordinates for a reappraise>watch type contrast) in the main article. The paper focuses on PPI connectivity and ROI-extracted beta coupling estimates, and refers to prior work and Supplement for broader results. Because the review requires at least one whole-brain task-evoked statistical map, this paper meets exclusion criterion E5 (only seed-based/ connectivity analyses reported without a whole-brain task activation map) and therefore must be excluded. Inclusion criteria met: I5, I6, I7, I8, I9. Inclusion criterion not met: I10 (whole-brain evidence).

This is a task-based fMRI study of instructed emotion regulation using cognitive reappraisal (reappraise vs view) with visual stimuli (IAPS images). Participants are adolescent girls (clinical PTSD sample) and analyses include within-task contrasts related to regulation (reappraise > view; view negative > view neutral). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise analyses (task-modulated functional connectivity contrasts with clusterwise inference and reported clusters/figures; supplementary figures provide task activation maps), and results are reported with clusters/coordinates. No exclusion criteria apply (not a review, not ROI-only, not resting-state-only, not between-group-only, not an empathy task). Full text includes introduction, methods, results and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria are violated.

Excluded because the study reports only ROI-based task analyses and does not provide any group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps or peak coordinates (Exclusion E4). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (an instructed emotion-regulation strategy was used — recall of positive autobiographical memories), I7 (visual emotional stimuli were used in the view condition — IAPS pictures), I8 (sample qualifies — healthy human participants), I9 (within-task contrasts reported, e.g. regulate > baseline, view > baseline, regulate > view). Inclusion criterion not met: I10 (no whole-brain group-level task activation maps / peak coordinates reported; task results are reported as ROI analyses). Full text appears complete.

Although this is a task-based fMRI study of instructed cognitive reappraisal using visual stimuli in children (meets I5, I6, I7, I8), the published results focus exclusively on seed-based task functional connectivity (PPI) analyses and do not report any group-level whole-brain task-evoked activation maps or peak coordinates in standard space. This study therefore reports only seed-based connectivity/effective connectivity results without accompanying whole-brain activation maps, which meets exclusion criterion E5. Inclusion criteria I9 and I10 (within-task whole-brain activation contrasts and whole-brain peak coordinates) are not satisfied in the provided full text.

This full text meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis: it is a task-based fMRI study (I5) that instructs an emotion regulation strategy (cognitive reappraisal Reduce vs Maintain; I6), uses visual stimuli (IAPS images; I7), includes adolescents with MDD and matched healthy controls with control results reported separately (I8), reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (Maintain vs Reduce, Reduce vs Maintain; I9), and presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with corrected cluster thresholds and coordinate-based reporting plus ROI analyses (I10). Reporting of whole-brain results in text/tables meets I11. The full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) are violated. Therefore include.

This is a task-based fMRI study with instructed cognitive reappraisal of visual (video) stimuli and reports results separately for SAD patients and healthy controls (meets I5, I6, I7, I8). However, the paper presents ROI-based network (DEPNA) connectivity analyses and does not report any group-level whole-brain, voxelwise task-activation maps with peak coordinates in standard space. Thus it fails the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked results (I10 not met). Because the imaging results are reported only as ROI/seed-based connectivity (DEPNA) without accompanying whole-brain activation maps, this study meets exclusion criteria E4 and E5 (ROI-only/partial-coverage/connectivity-only reporting). Also, the paper does not provide the conventional within-task whole-brain activation contrasts (e.g., reappraise > look) as voxelwise maps (I9 not satisfied for whole-brain contrast reporting). Therefore it should be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study using instructed cognitive reappraisal (REAL/PHOTO/LOOK cues) with visual stimuli (IAPS and photos). It reports within-task contrasts of reappraisal conditions (e.g., negative/real vs negative/photo) and whole-brain voxelwise analyses with corrected clusters and ROI analyses, and provides full methods, results, and discussion. The sample includes unmedicated MDD patients and healthy controls with separate reporting. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs participants to engage in self-referential emotion regulation (imagining experiencing positive-social scenes), i.e., an instructed regulation strategy (up-regulation via perspective-taking). Stimuli are visual (IAPS/NAPS/GAPED images). The sample is a healthy volunteer group with group-level results reported. The paper reports within-task contrasts (regulation > viewing; positive > neutral; task × stimulus interaction) and whole-brain group-level voxelwise analyses with peak coordinates (FWE-corrected), satisfying reporting requirements. Full text contains Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I11 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This full-text reports a task-based fMRI study that explicitly instructed cognitive reappraisal (reappraisal vs attend blocks) in adolescents during visual stimuli (photos of peers). It includes behavioral and neural analyses with the key within-task contrast (reappraisal > attend) and reports whole-brain group-level results with peak coordinates (right frontal pole, BA9/BA10) and cluster statistics. Both depressed and non-depressed groups are reported and compared. Thus all inclusion criteria are met (I5–I11). No exclusion criteria apply: the study is empirical, includes whole-brain activation analyses (not only ROI or connectivity), reports within-task effects, and is not an empathy/perspective-taking study without regulation instructions. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion).

This is a task-based fMRI study that directly instructs participants to regulate emotional responses (explicit up-regulation via instructed imitation, IMT, and down-regulation via expressive suppression, eSUP) while viewing visual emotional stimuli (dynamic face video clips). It reports within-task contrasts relevant to regulation (IMT > eSUP, IMT > GND, eSUP > IMT, etc.) and conducts group-level, whole-brain random-effects SPM analyses with coordinates and cluster reporting. The sample (20 healthy adults) is acceptable, and the full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not a review, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-task effects, not an empathy task without regulation). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10, and I11 and is appropriate for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

The paper is a task-based fMRI study that instructs participants to use cognitive reappraisal (reinterpretation) to down-regulate negative emotion (meets I5 and I6). Stimuli are visual IAPS pictures (I7). Sample is healthy adults (I8). The paper reports within-task contrasts relevant to regulation (Reappraise > Negative and Negative > Reappraise) (I9). Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses are reported with FDR correction and coordinates/tables/figures (I10,I11). Full text includes introduction, methods, results and discussion; no exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria.

This study meets the review inclusion criteria: it is a task-based fMRI experiment (I5) that instructs cognitive reappraisal as the regulation strategy (Regulate vs Attend; I6). The regulated stimuli are visual (colored CS squares and cigarette images; I7). The sample (adult smokers) is acceptable per criteria (I8). The paper reports within-task contrasts directly assessing regulation (Attend CS+ vs Regulate CS+; I9). Group-level, whole-brain random-effects statistical maps were computed and thresholded (p<0.001) after normalization to standard (MNI) space, and activations (including right dACC, BA24/32) are reported in the text/figures, satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements (I10, I11). The full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria apply.

This full text clearly meets all inclusion criteria: it is a task-based fMRI study (I5) that instructs emotion regulation strategies (increase/decrease via cognitive reappraisal/distancing) during the task (I6); stimuli are visual IAPS images (I7); sample includes clinical groups and healthy controls with results reported separately (I8); analyses report within-task contrasts (increase>maintain, decrease>maintain) (I9); group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported with cluster-level correction and peak coordinates (I10); results are presented in text/tables with coordinates (I11). No exclusion criteria apply: the study reports whole-brain task activation maps (not only ROI or connectivity) and includes within-group task effects. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Full text reports an empirical task-based fMRI study in which participants were instructed to use a cognitive reappraisal strategy (detachment) to regulate emotions elicited by visual stimuli (IAPS pictures). Methods and results include within-task contrasts of regulation versus no-regulation (e.g., negative regulation > no regulation), whole-brain group-level voxelwise analyses with corrected thresholds and peak coordinates, and separate patient and healthy control group reporting. The paper also reports psychophysiological interaction analyses but not as the sole analysis. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so is complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met (I5–I11) and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs participants to use cognitive reappraisal (increase, decrease, maintain) during recall of previously encoded visual images (IAPS). Methods report whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (SPM8) with coordinates/tables and contrasts relevant to regulation (e.g., decrease>maintain, increase>maintain, conjunctions, phase-specific contrasts). Sample is healthy young adults and within-task contrasts are reported. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

Although this is an empirical, task-based fMRI paper with whole-brain group-level results (meets I5, I8, I10, I11), it does NOT meet key topical inclusion criteria for this meta-analysis. The fMRI task is a placebo analgesia paradigm using thermal pain stimuli and expectancy manipulation, not an instructed emotion-regulation task with visual emotional stimuli. The independent cognitive reappraisal (CRA) lab task using visual images was performed outside the scanner and not used as an in-scanner regulation instruction; there is no within-fMRI contrast of an instructed regulation condition (e.g. reappraise > look) nor any visual-emotion stimulus regulation in the scanner. Therefore inclusion criteria I6, I7 and I9 are not satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply. Full text appears complete.

The full text describes a task-based fMRI experiment in which participants were instructed to use emotion regulation strategies (cognitive reappraisal and expressive suppression) while viewing visual stimuli (Chinese Affective Picture System images). The paper reports within-task contrasts (reappraisal vs. watch; suppression vs. watch; watch-negative vs. watch-neutral) and group-level whole-brain analyses with peak MNI coordinates and FWE-corrected thresholds, along with ROI/SVC analyses. Methods (participants, stimuli, fMRI acquisition, preprocessing, GLM) and results (behavioral, activation, PPI) are fully reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not only ROI-only, not only connectivity, empirical, includes within-task effects). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that directly matches the review objective. It instructs cognitive emotion regulation (socially-induced reappraisal/distancing) during presentation of visual emotional stimuli (IAPS pictures), reports within-task contrasts (Social-Reg > Social-Look; Self-Reg > Self-Look), and presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise results with peak coordinates and cluster-level FWE correction. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I11 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria are met.

This is a task-based fMRI study in which participants were explicitly instructed to apply emotion-regulation strategies (cognitive reappraisal, suppression, up-regulation) while viewing visual stimuli (static high-calorie food images). The manuscript reports within-subject contrasts comparing regulation conditions (e.g., suppression vs. reappraisal, up-regulation vs. suppression) and describes a group-level, whole-brain RFX ANOVA with corrected F-map and identified fROIs in standard space. The sample (healthy adult women) is eligible. Reporting of whole-brain results and task contrasts satisfies the meta-analysis inclusion requirements. Full text (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion) is present and sufficient for screening. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study that directly compares instructed emotion-processing/acceptance ("permit") with passive viewing of visual emotional stimuli (IAPS). It meets inclusion criteria: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (instruction to permit/accept emotion—an antecedent-focused/acceptance strategy), I7 (visual stimuli—static IAPS pictures), I8 (healthy adult sample reported), I9 (within-task contrasts reported, e.g., permit > view, view negative > view neutral), I10 (group-level whole-brain random-effects analyses with voxelwise results and FWE-corrected clusters reported), and I11 (whole-brain results described in text/tables/figures). No exclusion criteria are met: the paper is empirical with whole-brain task activation maps and within-group contrasts; it is not limited to ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, nor is it an empathy-perspective-taking-only task. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Full text reports an empirical task-based fMRI study that instructs cognitive reappraisal (DECREASE vs LOOK) during presentation of visual IAPS images (static pictures). Sample and methods are appropriate; within-task regulation contrasts (decrease-negative > look-negative) and unregulated viewing contrasts (look-negative > look-neutral) are reported. Group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (FWE-corrected maps and peak coordinates cited). Full article (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I11 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of explicit emotion regulation using instructed strategies (reappraisal and response modulation) with visual stimuli (IAPS pictures). The paper reports within-task contrasts (e.g., regulate > maintain, increase > decrease) and provides group-level whole-brain voxelwise results with MNI peak coordinates for amygdala and PFC clusters. The sample (healthy young adults) is eligible and the full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not non-empirical, and not an empathy/perspective-taking task without regulation). Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I11 are satisfied and the study should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis. It is a task-based fMRI study (I5) that instructed emotion regulation (look, increase, decrease) using cognitive reappraisal strategies (I6). Stimuli were visual (IAPS and in-house disgusting images) (I7). The sample includes children/adolescents with ASD and TD controls (I8). The paper reports within-task regulation contrasts (decrease-gross vs. look-gross; increase-gross vs. look-gross) (I9). It performed group-level, whole-brain random-effects GLM analyses and references coordinate tables/figures (Table S2, figures) satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements (I10,I11). No exclusion criteria apply: the study is empirical with original fMRI task activation maps (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only), and includes within-group task effects. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study reports a task-based fMRI experiment (Experiment 3) in which participants were instructed to cognitively reappraise visual emotional stimuli (IAPS images) with explicit Increase/Maintain/Decrease instructions. It reports within-task contrasts (e.g., Increase > Maintain, Decrease > Maintain), whole-brain group-level activation results with peak coordinates and corrected thresholds, and provides full methods and results. Participant sample is healthy adults. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply.

Excluded because the regulated stimuli are script-driven verbal narratives (script-driven imagery/word/sentence stimuli), not visual stimuli; thus the study fails inclusion criterion I7. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (instructed cognitive reappraisal task), I8 (sample reporting patient and control groups), I9 (within-task contrasts reported: UP>maintain, DOWN>maintain), I10 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported), I11 (whole-brain results presented in tables/supplement). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore EXCLUDED solely for not meeting I7 (non-visual, script-driven stimuli).

This is a task-based fMRI study (N=51) that instructed explicit emotion regulation strategies (reappraisal and suppression) while participants viewed visual emotional stimuli (IAPS images). The paper reports within-task contrasts relevant to the review (View Negative > View Neutral; Reappraise > Attend Negative; Suppress > Attend Negative) and conducts group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with reported peak coordinates and tables. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not a review, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, contains within-task effects, not an empathy/perspective-taking-only design). Therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria I5–I11 and should be included in the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study that explicitly instructs a cognitive reappraisal strategy (distancing) and contrasts distance vs permit conditions. Stimuli are visual (abstract cues and targets in a monetary incentive delay task) that elicit reward-related emotional responses; regulation is instructed during anticipation (expectation) and outcome periods. The paper reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (Distance > Permit and related interactions), provides group-level voxelwise analyses with peak coordinates in standard MNI space (whole-brain/ROI analyses reported), and the full text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria are met: this is empirical, not connectivity-only, includes within-group task effects, and reports whole-brain voxelwise results. Full text appears complete. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the review.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study that instructs cognitive reappraisal during an emotion regulation task using visual stimuli (IAPS images). The manuscript reports within-task contrasts (Reappraise > Look; Reappraise > implicit baseline) and group-level whole-brain random-effects analyses with peak coordinates (e.g., left IFG), fulfilling whole-brain reporting. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and violates no exclusion criteria.

The study is a task-based fMRI investigation of instructed emotion regulation (reappraisal) using visual stimuli (IAPS images and facial displays) in an appropriate adult sample and reports within-task contrasts (Look vs Decrease; Match vs Label). However, all activation effects are reported using ROI-based analyses (amygdala ROIs) and PPI connectivity analyses restricted to anatomically defined IFG masks. The paper does not present any group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation maps (analyses were mask-restricted), so it fails inclusion criterion I10 and (by implication) I11. This violates exclusion criterion E4 (reports only ROI / small-volume-corrected results with no accompanying whole-brain analysis). Therefore the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study of instructed emotion regulation (cognitive reappraisal) using visual stimuli (food images) in an adolescent sample, and it reports within-task contrasts (e.g., reappraise > imagine eating) and whole-brain analyses. However, the provided full text does not report peak activation coordinates in a standard stereotaxic space (e.g., MNI or Talairach) or tables/figures with such coordinates, which is required by inclusion criterion I10 for coordinate-based meta-analysis. Therefore I cannot confirm that I10 is satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) are met in the provided content. Based on the absence of reported peak coordinates in the supplied full text, the study must be excluded for failure to meet all required inclusion criteria.

Although this is a task-based, within-subject fMRI study reporting whole-brain task activation maps and coordinates, it fails the review's stimulus criterion. The regulated emotional stimuli are experimenter-selected negative self-belief sentences (word/sentence stimuli presented on screen). The meta-analysis exclusion explicitly excludes studies whose regulated stimuli are word/sentence stimuli (I7 not met). Other inclusion criteria are satisfied (see list). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply. Full text appears complete.

All inclusion criteria are met: This is a task-based fMRI study (I5) that instructs a cognitive emotion regulation strategy (self-distancing/reappraisal) (I6). Regulated stimuli are visual IAPS pictures (I7). Sample is healthy participants (female young adults), qualifying under sample criteria (I8). The paper reports within-task regulation contrasts (e.g., Response: Attend > Distance; Prediction Error: Distance > Attend) (I9). Analyses are group-level, whole-brain voxelwise with cluster-level FWE correction and reported coordinates/tables (MNI coordinate(s) and Table S2 referenced), satisfying whole-brain evidence (I10) and acceptable reporting (I11). The full text provided includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false. No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, no connectivity-only, etc.). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED for the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study (I5) with an eligible sample (I8) that reports within-task contrasts (Tenderness vs Anguish) and provides group-level whole-brain, FWE-corrected results with peak coordinates (I9, I10). However, it does NOT meet key inclusion requirements: I6 (the task does not instruct a canonical emotion-regulation strategy applied to an external stimulus such as cognitive reappraisal/acceptance/reality-checking; participants were instructed to generate/up-regulate internal emotional states via personalized recall/mantras and neurofeedback) and I7 (the regulated/emotion-eliciting stimuli were primarily non-visual: music and autobiographical imagery; the virtual environment served as neurofeedback/BCI rather than as the visual emotional stimulus to be regulated). No exclusion criteria from the review (E3–E7) are directly triggered. Therefore the study is excluded because it fails to satisfy I6 and I7 required by the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs cognitive reappraisal using visual stimuli (film clips) and reports within-task contrasts (Regulate vs Attend). However, the paper reports ROI-based task activation analyses (extracted mean BOLD in predefined spherical ROIs) rather than a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked activation map with peak coordinates. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I10 (whole-brain task activation reporting) and meets exclusion criterion E4 (reports only ROI results with no accompanying whole-brain task analysis). Summary: exclusion criteria met: E4. Inclusion criteria met: I5, I6, I7, I8, I9. Inclusion criterion not met: I10. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a task-based fMRI study that explicitly instructed cognitive reappraisal via distancing to downregulate emotion (meets I5,I6). Stimuli were visual pictures (negative, positive, neutral), meeting I7. Sample includes acute AN patients and matched healthy controls with group results reported separately (I8). The paper reports within-task contrasts related to regulation and viewing (negative watch > neutral; negative watch > negative distance; negative watch < negative distance) (I9). Group-level voxelwise analyses and whole-brain/exploratory results with peak coordinates are reported (figures/Supplementary, coordinate peaks in text), satisfying I10 and I11. Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion; no exclusion criteria are met (not a review, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, contains within-group task effects, not an empathy task). Therefore the study is eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs participants to regulate affect (up-regulate by “thinking happy thoughts” and down-regulate by “relaxing”), reports within-task regulation contrasts (up vs down), includes a suitable sample (children/adolescents), and provides group-level whole-brain analyses (see main text and supplementary Table S4/Fig S2). However, the experimental regulation was directed at internallygenerated affect via neurofeedback rather than regulation of emotional responses to visual stimuli: the neurofeedback task did not present emotional visual stimuli during the regulation blocks (the visual faces were used only in the localiser), so the study does not meet the review’s requirement that the regulated stimuli be visual (I7). The meta-analysis objective specifically targets studies where participants regulate an emotional response to visual stimuli (or view them without regulating). Therefore, despite meeting several inclusion criteria, failure to meet I7 means exclusion.

This is a task-based fMRI study that explicitly instructed an emotion regulation strategy (cognitive reappraisal) using visual stimuli (96 IAPS images). The paper reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (Reappraise vs Maintain, Maintain vs Look) and provides peak coordinates (MNI) for activation and connectivity results, satisfying whole-brain, voxelwise reporting.
