This is a task-based fMRI study (I5) that instructed participants to perform an emotion-labeling task (affect labeling), which constitutes an instructed emotion-regulation strategy (I6). The emotional stimuli were visual (faces) (I7). The sample is a nonclinical adult sample reported separately (I8). The paper reports within-task contrasts relevant to regulation (emotion label > gender label) and an unregulated viewing contrast (observe > fixation) (I9). Group-level whole-brain analyses with peak coordinates are reported (I10) and results are presented in text/tables/figures (I11). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis and should be included.

Exclusion E4 applies: the study’s primary task activation results are reported using an a priori ROI (bilateral amygdala) rather than a group-level whole-brain task-evoked activation map with peak coordinates. Although a whole-brain PPI (connectivity) analysis is reported, the paper does not present a whole-brain voxelwise task-activation map (contrast of emotion viewing) with peaks in standard space. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli: faces), I8 (sample qualifies), I9 (reports an unregulated viewing contrast: fearful vs. happy). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no instructed emotion regulation strategy—the task was implicit gender discrimination, not reappraisal or other regulation), I10 (no group-level whole-brain task-evoked activation map reported), I11 (no whole-brain activation peaks/tables provided). Because I10/I11 are not satisfied and the paper relies on ROI results without a whole-brain task activation map, it does not meet the meta-analysis requirement for whole-brain task-evoked evidence and must be excluded.

This full text meets the review’s criteria for inclusion as an unregulated viewing fMRI study. It is a task-based fMRI study (I5) using visual emotional stimuli (I7: IAPS/static grayscale images) and includes an unregulated viewing contrast (Negative > Neutral) reported in voxel-wise, group-level whole-brain analyses (I9, I10). Results are presented in tables and figures with voxelwise thresholds and reported regions (I11). Sample includes a clinical group and controls (I8). The task was an emotional oddball requiring attention to targets amid emotional distractors; no instruction to regulate emotion was given, so the study does not meet I6 (instructed emotion regulation), but I6 is not required because the meta-analysis accepts unregulated viewing contrasts per I9. Full text is complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only results, connectivity-only analyses, or empathy/perspective-taking tasks) apply. Therefore the study is eligible for inclusion as an unregulated visual-emotion task with whole-brain activation contrasts.

Exclusion reason: E4 applies — the study reports amygdala task activation using small-volume correction (ROI/SVC) and does not report a whole-brain task-evoked group activation map for the emotion contrast. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I8 (eligible sample: healthy adult participants), I9 (reports a within-task contrast: sad vs neutral). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I6 (no instructed emotion regulation strategy — participants performed autobiographical memory recall, not reappraisal/acceptance or other instructed regulation), I7 (stimuli are script-driven autobiographical recall accompanied by music, not visual emotional stimuli such as pictures or film), I10 (no whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked activation map reported; primary activation was tested with SVC). Full text appears complete: fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructed participants to use distraction (MEMORIZE condition) versus passive viewing to regulate emotional responses to visual stimuli (IAPS and EmoPics), with female BPD patients and control groups reported separately. The analysis includes within-task contrasts (NEGATIVE>NEUTRAL; MEMORIZE vs VIEW) and group×time×task contrasts, and reports whole-brain voxelwise results with MNI peak coordinates. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5–I11 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is a task-based fMRI study using visual emotional face stimuli with patient and control groups and reports within-task contrasts (emotional conflict adaptation) with coordinate results; however it does NOT meet key inclusion requirements. The meta-analysis requires an instructed emotion regulation task (I6), e.g., reappraise vs look; here regulation is implicit/non-instructed (the study explicitly tests spontaneous, non-instructed adaptation), so I6 is not met. Additionally, the paper reports results only within a priori ROIs with small-volume correction and displays findings within those ROIs (no whole-brain voxelwise group-level activation map reported), thus failing the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked maps with peak coordinates (I10). This violates exclusion criterion E4 (ONLY ROI/SVC results reported). Therefore the study must be excluded.

This is a task-based fMRI study using visual stimuli (faces) with whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses and within-task contrasts of emotional viewing (e.g., fear > calm, early > late habituation). Thus it meets I5, I7, I8, I9, I10, and I11. However, participants were not instructed to use any emotion regulation strategy (e.g., reappraisal, distancing, acceptance); the task required detection/response suppression but did not instruct subjects to regulate their emotional responses. Therefore it does NOT meet I6 (an instructed emotion regulation strategy) and must be excluded. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) are met. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based (event-related) fMRI study using visual emotional stimuli (faces) and reports within-task unregulated viewing contrasts (angry>neutral, fearful>neutral, happy>neutral) with whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses and peak coordinates (FDR-corrected). Although no explicit emotion-regulation instruction was given (I6 not met), the meta-analysis objective explicitly accepts studies where participants view emotional stimuli without regulating; the study therefore satisfies the unregulated-viewing criterion (I9). The full text is complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli), I8 (sample qualifies), I9 (reports unregulated viewing contrasts), I10 (whole-brain group-level analysis with coordinates), I11 (results clearly described). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply. Given these points, the study is appropriate for inclusion in the meta-analysis examining neural responses during viewing (unregulated) of visual emotional stimuli.

The study is EXCLUDED. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I8 (sample acceptable). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I6 (no instructed emotion-regulation strategy; participants were not told to reappraise or otherwise regulate emotion), I7 (stimuli were auditory tones and white-noise UCS, not VISUAL stimuli), I9 (no within-task contrast of instructed emotion regulation or an unregulated visual-viewing contrast as required), I10 (analyses were restricted to anatomical ROIs rather than reporting a whole-brain, voxelwise group map). Exclusion criteria met: E4 (results are reported using ROI-restricted analyses with no accompanying whole-brain analysis). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study does not satisfy the review objective of fMRI studies of instructed regulation or viewing of visual emotional stimuli.

Exclusion: E5 applies — the study reports resting-state and seed-based functional connectivity analyses (amygdala connectivity) and does not provide a whole-brain task-evoked activation map relevant to instructed emotion regulation. Inclusion: I8 is satisfied (sample characteristics: female clinical BPD group and healthy controls reported separately). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I6 (no instructed emotion-regulation strategy such as reappraisal/distancing was employed), I7 (regulated stimuli are not visual emotional images; stress was induced via the Montreal Imaging Stress Task and incision, not visual emotional stimuli), I9 (no within-task contrast reflecting emotion regulation like “reappraise > look”), I10 (no group-level whole-brain task-evoked activation map reported), and I5 (while an fMRI task was used for stress induction, the study does not constitute a task-based emotion-regulation fMRI study as required by the review objective). Full text appears complete.

The study is a task-based fMRI investigation using visual emotional stimuli (IAPS) and reports within-task contrasts comparing negative versus neutral trials (attending and ignoring conditions). It provides group-level whole-brain random-effects analyses with MNI coordinates and tables/figures, and the full text includes methods, results, and discussion. Although no explicit emotion-regulation instruction (reappraisal) was used, the review objective allows unregulated viewing contrasts (e.g., emotion > neutral), which this paper reports. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, empathy/perspective-taking-only, or non-empirical) apply. Full text appears complete.

Exclusion E5 applies: the study reports only seed-based task connectivity (amygdala seed) results rather than whole-brain task-evoked activation maps. Although it contains a task contrast (Violence > Non-Violence) and reports voxelwise connectivity maps with peak coordinates, these are connectivity (seed-to-voxel) analyses and no conventional whole-brain task activation (e.g., emotion > neutral) activation map is reported. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli: violent video game clips), I8 (eligible sample), I9 (reports within-task unregulated viewing contrast analogue, PLAC Violence > PLAC Non-Violence), I10 (group-level voxelwise maps with MNI coordinates provided for connectivity results), I11 (results described in text/tables). Inclusion criteria not met: [] (none additionally unmet beyond the connectivity-only issue). Full text appears complete.

This study is EXCLUDED because it does not meet inclusion criterion I6: participants were not instructed to use an emotion-regulation strategy (e.g., reappraisal, distancing, acceptance). Instead, the task required attending to and classifying visual stimuli (face/scene valence), probing implicit emotion regulation. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli: faces and scenes), I8 (sample includes adolescents), I9 (reports within-task contrasts/unregulated viewing contrasts such as threatening > neutral), I10 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with MNI coordinates and cluster correction), and I11 (whole-brain results clearly reported). Exclusion criteria met: none (E3–E7 not applicable). Because at least one required inclusion criterion (I6) is not satisfied, the study must be excluded from this meta-analysis.

Full text is complete. Excluded because the study does not meet key inclusion criteria for this meta-analysis: although it is a task-based whole-brain fMRI study (I5) with an eligible sample (I8) and reports group-level whole-brain results (I10) and acceptable reporting (I11), it does NOT instruct an emotion-regulation strategy (I6 not met). The paradigm used math and word verification tasks that incidentally evoke anxiety rather than instructions to reappraise or otherwise regulate emotional responses; stimuli are cognitive problems rather than visual emotional stimuli of the type required (I7 not met). The paper also does not report within-task contrasts specifically labeling instructed emotion regulation (I9 not met). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply.

The article is a task-based fMRI study that instructs participants to use a cognitive reappraisal strategy (reinterpretation) to downregulate desire for visually presented food images. It reports within-task contrasts (REGULATE_TASTY > ADMIT_TASTY) and group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with peak coordinates in MNI space. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. All inclusion criteria I5–I11 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

The study is a task-based fMRI investigation using visual IAPS pictures, with patient and healthy control groups and within-task contrasts (e.g. negative > neutral), so it meets I5, I7, I8, and I9. However, participants were instructed to anticipate and view stimuli rather than to use an instructed emotion-regulation strategy (I6 not met). Critically, the fMRI analysis was a hypothesis-driven ROI analysis (predefined spherical ROIs) and the paper reports ROI beta-weights rather than group-level whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps or peak coordinates; thus it fails I10 and meets exclusion criterion E4 (ONLY ROI results, no whole-brain analysis). Because E4 is met and key inclusion criteria (I6 and I10) are not satisfied, the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based whole-brain fMRI study (I5) of schizophrenia patients and matched controls (I8). It reports within-task emotion contrast (negative vs neutral olfactory stimulation) (I9) and provides group-level whole-brain results with peak coordinates/tables (I10, I11). However, it does NOT meet critical eligibility requirements for this review: the emotional stimuli are olfactory (odorants), not VISUAL, so I7 is not met. Also, participants were not instructed to regulate their emotional responses (no emotion-regulation instruction such as reappraisal/acceptance/distancing), so I6 is not met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply to this report. Because inclusion criteria I6 and I7 are not satisfied, the study is excluded.

This full-text reports a task-based fMRI experiment that instructed participants to regulate emotion (explicit 'Regulate' vs 'Look' instructions using cognitive-linguistic reappraisal strategies), used visual stimuli (static photographs of harsh faces and violent scenes), included both a clinical group (SAD) and a demographically-matched healthy control group with results reported separately, and presents within-task contrasts relevant to emotion regulation (e.g. Regulate > Look; Look Harsh Face > Neutral) with group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses and peak coordinates in Talairach space. The full article includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion (i.e., the full text appears complete). No exclusion criteria are met.

This is a task-based fMRI study using visual emotional stimuli (IAPS images) with an emotional picture-processing task and explicit contrasts comparing negative, positive, and neutral conditions. Although participants were not instructed to apply an emotion-regulation strategy, the study reports within-task unregulated viewing contrasts (e.g., negative expected pictures vs neutral/positive) at the group level and provides whole-brain, voxelwise second-level analyses with reported significant clusters and coordinates. The sample includes a patient group (Takotsubo) and matched healthy controls reported separately. The full text contains methods, results, and discussion, and whole-brain results are reported in tables/figures. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria for studies that examine viewing (unregulated) of visual emotional stimuli and provides whole-brain task activation results suitable for the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study using an instructed cognitive reappraisal paradigm (Observe, Maintain, Suppress) with visual stimuli (IAPS images). It reports within-task contrasts relevant to emotion regulation (Maintain>Observe; Suppress>Maintain) and provides group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with MNI coordinates and tables/figures. Both cocaine-dependent and control groups are reported separately. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, allowing complete assessment. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study (I5) that instructs participants to regulate emotional responding (upregulate left amygdala during a happy memory induction; I6), includes an eligible sample (MDD patients; I8), reports within-task contrasts (Happy Memories vs Rest/Count; I9), and provides whole-brain group-level voxelwise analyses and coordinates (PPI and group maps; I10). However, the regulated emotional stimuli are internally generated autobiographical memories rather than externally presented visual emotional stimuli (no IAPS/images/film/video stimuli), so it does not meet I7 (visual emotional stimuli). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply. Therefore the study must be excluded because it fails to meet inclusion criterion I7 (visual stimuli).

This is a task-based fMRI study using visual emotional stimuli (sad and neutral film clips) and reports within-task unregulated viewing contrasts (Sad > Neutral). Whole-brain group-level analyses are reported with peak coordinates in standard space, and the full article includes methods, results, and discussion. The study therefore meets the review’s scope (studies of viewing visual emotional stimuli without regulation) and satisfies inclusion criteria I5, I7, I8, I9, I10, and I11. No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study using visual emotional stimuli (fearful and neutral faces) and reports within-task contrasts of unregulated viewing (fearful > neutral) at the group level. Whole-brain group analyses with peak coordinates in standard space are reported. Sample includes a clinical PTSD group and traumatized controls reported separately. Although no instructed emotion-regulation strategy was used (I6 not met), the protocol and reported contrasts satisfy the meta-analysis objective by providing unregulated viewing contrasts. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text is complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study using visual emotional face stimuli and an instructed effortful regulation paradigm (n-back with emotional distractors), reporting within-task contrasts and MNI coordinates; however all neuroimaging analyses were conducted within an a priori region-of-interest mask (frontolimbic and striatal ROIs) and no whole-brain, group-level voxelwise activation maps or analyses are reported. Per the review criteria, studies that report ONLY ROI or small-volume-corrected results with no whole-brain analysis must be excluded (E4). Inclusion criteria satisfied: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (instructed cognitive control/effortful emotion regulation via task demands), I7 (visual stimuli—faces), I8 (sample acceptable), I9 (within-task contrasts reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I10 (no whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task activation map reported). Full text appears complete.

This study is a task-based fMRI investigation (I5) using visual stimuli (animated Cyberball; I7) in an adolescent sample (I8). It reports within-task contrasts of unregulated viewing (observed inclusion vs observed exclusion; I9) and presents whole-brain, group-level results with peak coordinates and tables (I10, I11). However, the study did NOT instruct participants to use any emotion regulation strategy (no reappraisal, distancing, acceptance, or other instructed regulation), so it fails inclusion criterion I6 (an instructed emotion-regulation task). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) appear to be met. Because ALL inclusion criteria must be satisfied and I6 is not met, the study must be excluded from this meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study using visual, static disorder-related and neutral scene stimuli presented during a feature-based task (CDTD). The paper reports within-task contrasts of unregulated viewing (disorder-related > neutral) and an exploratory whole-brain analysis with reported activation clusters/tables, and includes both a clinical (SAD) group and healthy controls. No instructed emotion-regulation strategy was used, but the review objective allows inclusion of studies that merely view visual emotional stimuli without regulation. Therefore the study meets the meta-analysis criteria for unregulated viewing contrasts. No exclusion criteria are triggered.

This is a task-based (rtfMRI) experimental study that instructed participants to volitionally regulate anterior insula activity using an instructed strategy (recalling/imagining negative personal events) and then presented visual emotional stimuli (painful pictures). The paper reports within-task contrasts (regulation > baseline), whole-brain group-level activation maps with MNI coordinates and appropriate corrections, and includes full methods, results, and discussion. Sample and analyses meet inclusion requirements. Full text appears complete.

This study is excluded because it does not meet inclusion criterion I6: participants were not instructed to employ an emotion regulation strategy. Instead, subjects performed a spatial cueing task and were told that faces were irrelevant (i.e., passive/ignored viewing), so no instructed regulation (reappraisal, distancing, acceptance, etc.) occurred. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual emotional stimuli — faces), I8 (sample acceptable — older and young adults), I9 (reports within-task contrasts for unregulated viewing; emotion vs neutral), I10 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with peak coordinates reported), I11 (results described adequately). Exclusion criteria met: none (no E3–E7 violations). Full text appears complete. Therefore excluded solely due to failure to meet I6 (instructed emotion regulation).

This is an original, task-based fMRI study using an instructed emotion-regulation manipulation (guided attentional distraction vs evaluation) with visual, static OCD-relevant and aversive images. The paper reports within-task contrasts (evaluation > distraction; OCD-relevant > neutral/aversive) and group-level, whole-brain analyses (with ROI follow-up), with results presented in figures and supplementary tables. Both patient and matched healthy control groups are reported separately. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not non-empirical, and includes within-group task effects). Full text contains introduction, methods, results and discussion, so it is complete. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of fMRI studies of instructed regulation (visual stimuli) and is included.

Although this is a task-based fMRI study using visual stimuli (Cyberball) and reports whole-brain group analyses of a within-task contrast (rejection > acceptance), it does not meet the requirement that an emotion-regulation strategy be instructed during the task. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli), I8 (eligible sample), I9 (reports within-task/unregulated viewing contrast: rejection>acceptance), I10 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with coordinates), I11 (results clearly described). Inclusion criterion not met: I6 (no instructed emotion-regulation strategy; the study assesses dispositional mindfulness rather than instructing participants to regulate). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) are triggered. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructed cognitive reappraisal (‘distance’) and ‘immerse’ conditions using visual IAPS images. The paper reports within-task contrasts relevant to the review (distance/aversive > immerse/aversive; immerse/aversive > immerse/neutral) and provides group-level whole-brain analyses with MNI coordinates. The full text includes methods, results, and discussion, and no exclusion criteria apply. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

Although this is a task-based fMRI study using visual emotional stimuli and an instructed cognitive-control task (EFNBACK) with appropriate within-task contrasts (e.g., emotional-distracter vs. no-distracter) and reported MNI peak coordinates, the reported activation results are restricted to predefined ROIs with ROI-based multiple-comparison correction (AlphaSim) and PPI analyses constrained to target ROIs. The paper does not present or report a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation map or whole-brain coordinates outside ROI-restricted results. This meets exclusion criterion E4 (ROI-only results with no accompanying whole-brain analysis). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (instructed cognitive control of emotional response via ignoring emotional distracters), I7 (visual stimuli), I8 (eligible sample), I9 (within-task contrasts reported), and I11 (coordinates reported for ROI clusters). Inclusion criterion not met: I10 (no whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked group map reported). Consequently the study is excluded.

This study is excluded because it does not meet key inclusion criteria for the review. (a) Exclusion IDs met: none. (b) Inclusion IDs met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I8 (sample reported with patient and control groups), I9 (within-task contrasts: stress > neutral reported), I10 (whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked analyses with MNI coordinates), I11 (results and coordinates clearly reported). (c) Inclusion IDs not met: I6 (no instructed emotion-regulation strategy — participants engaged in script-driven imagery without instructions to reappraise, accept, or otherwise regulate emotion), I7 (stimuli are script-driven auditory imagery, not visual stimuli such as pictures or films). Because the meta-analysis requires instructed emotion-regulation tasks of visual stimuli, failure to meet I6 and I7 warrants exclusion. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that instructs emotion regulation (explicit suppression) and uses priming for implicit suppression during viewing of visual emotional stimuli (IAPS and other images). The paper reports within-task contrasts comparing suppression runs to baseline (e.g., EXP vs BASEEXP), Dm (subsequent memory) contrasts, group-level random-effects whole-brain analyses with tables/clusters and ROI analyses, and peak coordinates. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (I5–I11) and violates no exclusion criteria. The full text appears complete.

This is a task-based, whole-brain fMRI study that directly examines instructed emotion regulation (reappraise > look) and uninstructed viewing (look negative > look neutral) using visual IAPS images. It reports within-task contrasts (reappraise > look; look negative > look neutral) at the group level with whole-brain voxelwise analyses and thresholding, and presents coordinate-based results. Sample is healthy adults. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis. It is a task-based fMRI study (I5) that instructs participants to use a cognitive emotion-regulation strategy (positive reappraisal) during the Picture Viewing Task (I6). The regulated stimuli are visual IAPS images (I7). The sample (clinical participants; transdiagnostic emotional distress disorders) is acceptable (I8). The paper reports within-task regulation contrasts (Positive Reappraisal vs Negative Attend) and relates activation to behavior (I9). Analyses are whole-brain, voxelwise group-level maps using FSL/FLAME with cluster correction and reported results/tables and supplemental figures (I10,I11). No exclusion criteria are met: results are not ROI-only, not limited to connectivity/resting-state, not only between-group contrasts, and it is not an empathy/perspective-taking task without regulation. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore include for the meta-analysis.

The study is a task-based fMRI with visual stimuli (peer face photographs) in adolescents, reports within-task contrasts (negative vs. positive feedback) and whole-brain results with peak coordinates. However, participants were not instructed to use any emotion regulation strategy (e.g., reappraisal, distancing, acceptance); the task probed natural responses to social feedback rather than instructed regulation. Thus it fails inclusion criterion I6 (no instructed emotion-regulation strategy). It meets I5, I7, I8, I9, I10, and I11 but not I6, so it must be excluded per the review criteria.

The study is excluded because it does not instruct participants to use an emotion regulation strategy (I6 not met). It is a task-based fMRI study (I5 met), uses visual stimuli (colored squares) (I7 met), includes an eligible sample of healthy adults (I8 met), reports within-task contrasts (CS- > CS+ and CS+ > CS-) that qualify as unregulated viewing contrasts (I9 met), and provides group-level whole-brain task analyses with coordinates (I10 and I11 met). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) are triggered. Full text appears complete. Because the review requires all inclusion criteria be met and this paper lacks instructed emotion regulation, it must be excluded.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that directly tests instructed cognitive reappraisal (enhance vs. suppress) using visual emotional stimuli (IAPS images). The paper reports within-task contrasts (enhance–suppress) for the emotion regulation fMRI session, conducts whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (FLAME) with cluster correction, and reports peak coordinates in MNI space (Tables and figures). Participant sample is a healthy group of males (acceptable per I8). Thus all required inclusion criteria for the review are met (I5–I11). No exclusion criteria apply: the study is not non-empirical, does not report only ROI or connectivity results, and includes within-group task effects rather than only between-group contrasts. Full text appears complete with introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Recommendation: INCLUDE in the meta-analysis. If desired, extract the reported whole-brain peak coordinates (Tables 1 & 2) and the (enhance> suppress) contrasts for coordinate-based meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study using visual emotional stimuli (IAPS) presented as distractors during a delayed working-memory task. The paper reports unregulated viewing contrasts (negative emotional > scrambled) and within-group as well as between-group whole-brain, voxelwise analyses with peak coordinates (FWE-corrected), and provides full methods, results and discussion. The sample includes OCD patients and matched healthy controls with within-group effects reported. Although no explicit emotion-regulation instruction (e.g., reappraisal) was given, the meta-analysis objective allows inclusion of studies that view emotional stimuli without regulating; the study therefore provides an appropriate unregulated emotion contrast for inclusion. Connectivity analyses (DCM) are present but whole-brain task activations are also reported, so exclusion criterion E5 does not apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Full-text provides a complete task-based fMRI study in which participants (AUD sample) performed instructed emotion-regulation tasks using visual stimuli (IAPS and alcohol/food images). The paper reports within-task contrasts for regulation (REAPPRAISE-Negative > LOOK-Negative; LATER > NOW) and whole-brain group-level activation maps with peak coordinates and cluster correction, plus tables/figures. All inclusion criteria (I5–I11) are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply. The ER task directly matches the meta-analysis objective (regulated vs. unregulated viewing of visual emotional stimuli).

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs emotion regulation (detach vs permit), uses visual stimuli (IAPS/EmoPicS), includes within-task contrasts for emotion reactivity and regulation (e.g., permit negative > permit neutral; detach negative > permit negative), reports whole-brain exploratory analyses with results/tables, and uses an eligible sample. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I5–I11. No exclusion criteria apply (not a review; includes whole-brain task activation maps and within-task effects; not only connectivity or ROI-only). Full text appears complete (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, References).

This is a task-based fMRI study using visual emotional stimuli (IAPS photographs) and reports within-task unregulated viewing contrasts (Negative > Neutral and arousal-specific contrasts) analyzed at the group level with whole-brain random-effects maps and reported peak coordinates. The sample (young and older adults) is acceptable. Although the reported results focus on a spontaneous viewing/run before any instructed emotion-regulation manipulation (so no instructed reappraisal contrast is analyzed here), the meta-analysis objective explicitly includes studies that view stimuli without regulating; therefore the study meets the relevant inclusion path. Inclusion criteria satisfied: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli), I8 (acceptable sample), I9 (reports within-task unregulated viewing contrasts), I10 (group-level whole-brain analyses), I11 (coordinates/results clearly described). No exclusion criteria were met. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study that directly addresses the review question. It uses an instructed emotion-regulation paradigm (LOOK/DECREASE) employing cognitive reappraisal instructions (I6) with visual stimuli from the IAPS (I7). The sample includes a clinical group (IGD) and matched controls reported separately (I8). Results include within-task effects (eg, negative vs neutral, look vs decrease; amygdala ROI and within-group comparisons) and contrasts related to regulation (I9). A group-level, whole-brain voxelwise GLM was conducted and reported with voxel-level thresholding and pFWE correction (voxel p<0.001, pFWE<0.05), with clusters reported in tables/figures (I10,I11). No exclusion criteria are met: the paper is empirical (not E3), reports whole-brain task activation (not E4 or E5), includes within-group task effects (not E6), and is not an empathy/perspective-taking study (not E7). Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

Although this is a task-based fMRI study using visual stimuli (partner facial expressions), reporting unregulated viewing contrasts (partner negative > partner neutral) and group-level whole-brain results with coordinates, it does NOT meet inclusion criterion I6: there was no instruction to regulate emotion (participants were explicitly not instructed to regulate). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete.

This study is a resting-state, seed-based connectivity fMRI investigation in adolescent marijuana users and does not involve a task or instructed emotion regulation. Exclusion criterion met: E5 (reports ONLY seed-based connectivity/resting-state analyses without a whole-brain task activation map). Inclusion criteria met: I8 (sample includes adolescents). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I5 (not a task-based fMRI study), I6 (no instructed emotion regulation/cognitive reappraisal), I7 (no visual emotional stimuli/task; resting-state), I9 (no within-task emotion-regulation or unregulated viewing contrasts), I10 (no group-level whole-brain task-evoked activation maps reported), I11 (not applicable as whole-brain task results are absent). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study does not address the review objective and must be excluded.

This full text meets all inclusion criteria: it is a task-based fMRI study (I5) that explicitly instructs cognitive reappraisal/downregulation (I6) of emotional responses to visual stimuli drawn from the IAPS (I7). Participants include clinical (bipolar I) and control groups with results reported separately (I8). The paper reports within-task contrasts relevant to regulation (decrease vs. observe) and unregulated viewing contrasts (observe negative vs. neutral) (I9). Group-level whole-brain random-effects analyses with thresholding and anatomical labeling are reported (cluster Z>2.0, p=.05 corrected), satisfying whole-brain reporting with standard-space localization (I10), and results are clearly described in text and tables/figures (I11). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) are met. The provided full text includes background, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. Therefore INCLUDE.

The study is a task-based fMRI investigation with whole-brain results and an appropriate sample (meets I5, I8, I9, I10, I11). However, it does NOT instruct an emotion-regulation strategy (no reappraisal/acceptance/distancing instructions) and thus fails I6. Crucially, the emotional stimuli are words (drug and neutral words), not visual images/film/clips; the review excludes studies using word/sentence stimuli, so it fails I7. No exclusion criteria from E3–E7 apply. Therefore the study must be excluded because it does not meet I6 and I7.

This is a task-based fMRI study using visual emotional stimuli (film clips) and reports within-task unregulated viewing contrasts (negative > neutral; positive > neutral) with group-level, voxelwise whole-brain results (cluster-corrected, MNI coordinates). The sample (children and adults) is eligible. Although no explicit emotion regulation instructions were given (i.e., I6 not satisfied), the meta-analysis objective accepts unregulated viewing contrasts; the study therefore satisfies the necessary inclusion conditions for unregulated viewing studies. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This study is a resting-state fMRI seed-based connectivity study using an acute tryptophan depletion challenge; it does not include any task-based emotion regulation paradigm or visual emotional stimuli. Exclusion criteria: E5 applies (reports ONLY resting-state/seed-based connectivity analyses without any task activation maps). Inclusion criteria met: I8 (sample description qualifies). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (not task-based fMRI), I6 (no instructed emotion regulation strategy), I7 (no visual emotional stimuli task), I9 (no within-task regulation or viewing contrasts), I10 (no whole-brain task-evoked group-level activation map). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the paper must be excluded from this meta-analysis focused on task-based emotion regulation fMRI.

This is a task-based fMRI study with visual emotional stimuli and whole-brain group analyses (meets I5, I7, I8, I9, I10, I11). However, participants were not instructed to regulate their emotional responses (no reappraisal/other instructed regulation); the task was an oddball target detection with aversive distractors, so inclusion criterion I6 (an instructed emotion-regulation strategy) is not met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study must be excluded because it fails to meet all required inclusion criteria (specifically I6).

This is an original, task-based fMRI study using a visual emotional task (approach–avoidance with happy/angry face images) in human participants (police recruits). The task includes explicit instructions requiring cognitive control over automatic emotional action tendencies (incongruent vs. congruent blocks), and the primary neural contrasts reported (incongruent > congruent) index instructed emotional control. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with peak MNI coordinates and FWE-corrected results, and also reports psychophysiological-interaction connectivity analyses. Methods, results, and discussion are present in full. Therefore the study meets the review’s requirements for task-based fMRI of instructed emotion regulation/control with visual stimuli and reports within-task contrasts and whole-brain results.

This study is excluded because it uses resting-state fMRI and multivariate machine learning to classify PTSD subtypes rather than a task-based emotion regulation paradigm. Exclusion criteria met: E5 (reports only resting-state analyses without any task-evoked whole-brain activation maps). Inclusion criteria met: I8 (sample: clinical and control groups reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (not a task-based fMRI study), I6 (no instructed emotion regulation strategy), I7 (no visual emotional stimuli used; resting-state, eyes-closed), I9 (no within-task emotion-regulation or viewing contrasts reported), I10 (no whole-brain task-evoked group-level task activation maps). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study does not address the review objective and must be excluded.

Exclusion E4 applies: the paper reports only ROI-masked group analyses (region-of-interest/full-factorial within an a priori relapse mask) and does not present a whole-brain, voxelwise group-level task activation analysis. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI with cue-exposure paradigms), I7 (visual stimuli: alcohol and neutral images), I8 (clinical sample acceptable), I9 (reports within-task contrast alcohol > neutral). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no instructed emotion regulation strategy; passive cue-reactivity, not reappraisal or other instructed regulation), I10 (no whole-brain voxelwise group analysis reported). Full text appears complete. Thus excluded because it fails I6 and I10 and meets exclusion E4.

This is a task-based fMRI study that directly investigates instructed cognitive control over emotional/ social-action tendencies using an approach-avoidance (AA) task. The AA task requires participants to override automatic emotional action tendencies (affect-incongruent vs affect-congruent), which constitutes an instructed emotion-regulation/cognitive-control strategy. Emotional stimuli are visual (faces). The paper reports within-task contrasts related to emotion regulation (incongruent > congruent) and links these to stress responsivity. Group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses were performed and reported (with peak coordinates and SVC ROI results), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked maps. The full text (background, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria apply. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study using visual emotional face stimuli and reports unregulated emotion contrasts, but it does not meet the meta-analysis requirement for whole-brain task-evoked activation reporting. Specifically, the paper focuses on ROI-based activation and dynamic causal modeling (effective connectivity) among vmPFC, sgACC, and amygdala, and does not present a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation map with peak coordinates. Therefore it falls under exclusions for ROI-only/effective-connectivity-only reporting.

This is a resting-state fMRI study (ALFF and seed-based rsFC) with no task, no instructed emotion-regulation paradigm, and no within-task contrasts or task-evoked activation maps. It therefore does not meet the review’s core inclusion requirements for a task-based emotion-regulation fMRI study. Exclusion criterion E5 applies because the paper reports only resting-state and connectivity/ALFF analyses without any whole-brain task activation maps. Inclusion criterion I8 (sample eligibility) is satisfied (older adult participants), but inclusion criteria I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (instructed emotion regulation task), I7 (visual emotional stimuli), I9 (within-task regulation or viewing contrasts), and I10 (whole-brain task-evoked maps) are NOT met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study is a task-based fMRI investigation of masked visual emotional faces in chronic marijuana smokers and controls (meets I5, I7, I8, I9, I10, I11). However, it does not instruct participants to use any emotion regulation strategy; subjects performed gender discrimination and passively viewed masked affective stimuli, with no reappraisal/acceptance/distancing or other instructed regulation (violates I6). No exclusion criteria from the list apply. Therefore the study must be excluded because it fails to meet inclusion criterion I6 (emotion-regulation instruction).

This study is a task-based fMRI investigation that instructs participants to exert cognitive control over emotional visual distractors (ignore emotional face distractors) during an N-back working memory task, which qualifies as instructed cognitive control of an emotional response. Stimuli are visual (faces). The paper reports within-task contrasts related to emotional processing (fearful>neutral; happy>neutral) and an interaction contrast linking emotional distractors with working-memory load, and conducts whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses with reported significant clusters (e.g., left IFG BA45). The sample includes a clinical group (schizophrenia) and healthy controls with results reported separately. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10, and I11 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

The study is a task-based fMRI investigation using visual emotional images and reports whole-brain group-level contrasts (negative > neutral) with coordinates, but the fMRI task did not instruct participants to use any emotion regulation strategy (it was an emotion identification/discrimination task). Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I6 (no instructed regulation), though it meets I5, I7, I8, I9, I10, and I11. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study of instructed emotion regulation in older adults that reports within-task contrasts and whole-brain voxelwise results. However, the regulated stimuli are personalized worry/suppression sentences (script-driven imagery / word/sentence prompts presented on the screen) rather than visual emotional stimuli (e.g., pictures, faces, film). Inclusion criterion I7 requires visual emotional stimuli and specifically excludes studies using word or sentence stimuli or purely script-driven imagery. Therefore the study fails to meet I7 and must be excluded. Included criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (instructed emotion regulation: worry suppression), I8 (eligible sample: elderly clinical + controls), I9 (reports within-task contrasts), I10 (whole-brain voxelwise maps), I11 (results reported in text/tables). Exclusion criteria met: none.

This is a task-based fMRI study with instructed emotion regulation (down-regulation via real-time fMRI neurofeedback) using visual aversive pictures in healthy participants, and it reports within-task contrasts (‘regulate > view’) in connectivity analyses. However, the paper presents only seed-based connectivity (PPI) and effective connectivity (DCM) results and does not report a group-level, whole-brain task activation map (task-evoked activation contrasts with whole-brain coordinates) within this full text (activation results are referenced as reported in a prior paper). Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E5 (ONLY seed-based/effective connectivity reported without a whole-brain task activation map). Inclusion criteria met: I5, I6, I7, I8, I9. Inclusion criterion not met: I10 (no whole-brain task-evoked activation map reported in this article). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion) so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is a task-based fMRI study of passive viewing of visual emotional stimuli (movie clips of fearful and neutral faces) with a clear within-task unregulated viewing contrast (negative > neutral). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (cluster-level FWE-corrected results with peak activations reported), and includes separate patient (BPD) and healthy control groups. Stimuli are visual; behavioural and imaging analyses include the relevant contrasts. Although no emotion-regulation instruction was given (i.e., I6 not met), the study provides an unregulated viewing contrast that satisfies the meta-analysis inclusion (I9). Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results and Discussion; supplemental material is not required. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I5, I7, I8, I9, I10 and I11 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is a task-based fMRI study using visual emotional stimuli (emotional faces) and reports within-task unregulated viewing contrasts (e.g., emotional face > fixation; happy/fearful vs. neutral). The sample (youth clinical and healthy controls) is eligible. The paper includes whole-brain (exploratory) group-level analyses (reported in supplemental Table S2) in standard space and provides coordinate-based results. Although the task did not instruct an emotion-regulation strategy (no reappraisal instruction), the meta-analysis objective explicitly accepts unregulated viewing contrasts; therefore the study meets the review’s eligibility (task-based visual emotional stimuli with within-task contrasts and whole-brain results). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, supplements referenced).

This study used resting-state seed-based functional connectivity in bipolar patients and did not include any task-based emotion regulation fMRI paradigm or visual emotional stimuli. Exclusion criterion E5 applies (reports only resting-state/seed-based connectivity without a task activation map). Inclusion criterion I8 (sample: clinical participants) is met. However it fails to meet required inclusion criteria I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (instructed emotion regulation strategy), I7 (visual emotional stimuli), I9 (within-task regulation/viewing contrast), and I10 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked activation maps). Full text appears complete and methods/results are provided, but the study does not address the meta-analysis objective of task-evoked emotion regulation to visual stimuli, so it must be excluded.

This is a task-based fMRI study (ER and CR tasks) that explicitly instructed an emotion regulation strategy (reappraise/savoring) during presentation of visual stimuli (IAPS and smoking images). The paper reports within-task contrasts (reappraise vs view; smoking cue vs neutral) entered into group-level repeated-measures random-effects analyses and describes significant group×time whole-brain effects (cluster-corrected) in rACC and ventral striatum, and reports seed-to-voxel rsFC analyses. Core sections (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion) are present, and whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed and reported (clusters within standard anatomical space), satisfying the review’s criteria. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is a task-based fMRI study in which participants were instructed to regulate emotion (compassion meditation vs. cognitive reappraisal) while viewing visual images from the IAPS. The fMRI task includes Regulate and Attend conditions, and analyses report Negative–Neutral contrasts and Post–Pre training contrasts. The paper reports both ROI and whole-brain voxel-wise analyses, including a significant whole-brain cluster with MNI coordinates in right AI/OFC, satisfying the requirement for whole-brain, group-level task activation maps. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis objective.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that instructed a cognitive emotion regulation strategy (imagery-based reappraisal) during presentation of visual stimuli (colored squares). The paper reports within-task contrasts directly addressing regulation (Attend vs Regulate CS+), uses group-level whole-brain GLM analyses with reported coordinates, and contains full methods, results, and discussion. Participants are healthy adults and analyses include SCR-behavior correlations. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I5–I11. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study (I5) using visual emotional stimuli (static facial expressions) (I7). Participants were explicitly instructed to try to become as happy or sad as possible using the faces (an instructed up-regulation/generation strategy), which meets the requirement for an instructed emotion-regulation strategy (I6) and/or qualifies for up-/down-regulation contrasts. The paper reports within-task contrasts of emotion versus baseline (sadness > baseline; happiness > baseline), satisfying the requirement for a within-task emotion regulation or unregulated viewing contrast (I9). Analyses were performed as group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise SPM2 analyses with cluster reporting and anatomical labeling (whole-brain task-evoked maps) consistent with I10; results are described and clusters reported in the text/tables (I11). The full text includes methods, results and discussion (fulltext_incomplete=false). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not non-empirical, and includes within-task effects). Therefore the study is eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study using visual emotional stimuli (dynamic faces) with an unregulated viewing contrast (emotions vs. shapes) reported. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses (FWE-corrected clusters) and provides region coordinates/cluster results. Sample includes clinical and healthy control groups. Although the task does not instruct an emotion regulation strategy (I6 not met), the study meets the meta-analysis’ allowance for unregulated viewing contrasts (I9). No exclusion criteria are met (not a review, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, contains within-task effects). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore it is eligible for inclusion under the unregulated viewing pathway.

This is a task-based fMRI study using visual stimuli (faces/houses) and reports task contrasts (AF and IF) with within-group results and clinical/control samples. However, all second-level analyses are restricted to a priori ROIs and results are reported from ROI clusters (no whole-brain, voxelwise group-level task activation map in standard space is provided). Therefore it violates exclusion criterion E4 (ONLY ROI/small-volume-corrected results with no whole-brain analysis). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli), I8 (sample qualifies), I9 (reports within-task contrasts/unregulated viewing contrasts). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no instructed emotion-regulation strategy such as reappraisal; task is an implicit attention/interference task rather than instructed regulation) and I10 (no whole-brain group-level voxelwise task activation reported). Full text appears complete.

Although this is a task-based, whole-brain fMRI study using visual face stimuli in an appropriate sample (I5, I7, I8, I10 satisfied), it does NOT instruct participants to regulate their emotional responses (I6 not met). The task involves impression formation and social-cognitive evaluation rather than an emotion-regulation instruction (e.g., reappraise, accept, distance). While condition>baseline contrasts were modeled for use in PLS, the study does not report within-task contrasts of emotion regulation nor an explicit unregulated viewing contrast of emotional stimuli (I9 not met). The study therefore falls outside the review scope; it also meets exclusion criterion E7 (social/perspective-taking/impression-formation without instruction to amplify or dampen one’s emotional response). Excluded because E7 applies; inclusion criteria met: I5, I7, I8, I10; inclusion criteria not met: I6, I9.

The study is a task-based fMRI experiment that instructs participants to use an attention-to-breath (ATB) mindfulness regulation strategy during presentation of aversive visual stimuli (IAPS). It reports within-task contrasts comparing regulation and passive viewing ([ATB vs PV], [PV vs ATB], picture vs no-picture), and links brain activation to behavioral regulation success. Whole-brain group-level analyses are reported (cluster/FWE thresholds) alongside ROI analyses and coordinate-based results. Sample is healthy adult participants and analyses include emotion-related contrasts and PPI connectivity but also whole-brain task activation maps. No exclusion criteria apply. Full text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present and sufficient for screening.

The full text describes an empirical task-based fMRI study using an instructed emotion regulation task (enhance/suppress/maintain) with visual stimuli (IAPS pictures). Within-task contrasts (positive suppress > positive maintain and negative suppress > negative maintain) are reported and used in hierarchical linear modeling to predict changes in anhedonia. Group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses are described with peak coordinates and cluster correction. The sample includes a clinical MDD group and a control group reported separately. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study satisfies all required inclusion criteria (I5–I11) and should be INCLUDED.

This is a task-based fMRI study that directly instructs participants to generate cognitive reappraisals (downregulate anger) — i.e., an emotion regulation strategy — satisfying the review focus on reappraisal. Emotional stimuli included photographs (presented with audio stories), qualifying as visual stimuli. The paper reports within-task contrasts (RGT > fixation; RGT > AUT) and whole-brain, voxelwise group analyses with voxelwise FWE correction and reported activation coordinates/figures. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria apply. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I11 are met and the study should be included.

This study should be excluded because it is not a task-based emotion regulation fMRI study. It uses resting-state fMRI effective connectivity (DCM) and diffusion MRI (DTI) tractography, with no instructed emotion-regulation task, no within-task regulation contrasts, and no whole-brain task-evoked activation maps. Exclusion criteria met: E5 (reports only resting-state/effective connectivity and structural analyses without any whole-brain task activation). Inclusion criteria met: I8 (sample includes clinical and control groups). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (instructed emotion regulation task), I9 (reports within-task regulation or viewing contrasts), I10 (whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps). Full text appears complete. Therefore excluded from the meta-analysis focusing on task-based emotion regulation fMRI.

This is a task-based fMRI study using visual emotional stimuli (face-matching with fear and neutral faces) and reports within-task unregulated viewing contrasts (fear > neutral, fear > neutral+control) at the group level. The paper includes full methods, results, and discussion; second-level whole-brain analyses and coordinate labeling are reported (tables/figures and supplementary material). The sample is described and eligible. The meta-analysis objective accepts either instructed regulation or unregulated viewing contrasts; this study supplies unregulated viewing contrasts appropriate for inclusion and does not violate any exclusion criteria (it is empirical, reports whole-brain task-evoked maps, and is not ROI-only or connectivity-only). Full text appears complete.

The study must be excluded because the regulated stimuli are script-driven imagery (participants imagined scenarios) rather than externally presented visual stimuli, so it fails inclusion criterion I7 (visual stimuli required). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (instructed emotion regulation: instructed suppression/'don't think'), I8 (acceptable sample), I9 (reports within-task regulation-related contrasts such as Don't Think > Think and Think Negative > Think Neutral), I10 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with peak coordinates), and I11 (whole-brain results clearly described). No exclusion criteria from E3–E7 apply. In summary: excluded because I7 not met (script-driven imagery/non-visual stimuli).

This is a task-based fMRI study that explicitly instructs emotion regulation (DECREASE trials using reappraisal/distancing strategies) during presentation of visual stimuli (static IAPS photographs). It reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (e.g. Decrease > Watch, Watch > Decrease) and presents group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses with peak coordinates in standard space (MNI, converted to Talairach). Sample and methods are described and the full article includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only reporting, no connectivity-only analyses, not a non-empirical paper, and the task includes instructed regulation rather than mere perspective-taking). Therefore the study meets all listed inclusion criteria (I5–I11).

The full text reports a task-based fMRI experiment that explicitly instructs emotion regulation (cognitive downregulation) during viewing of visual emotional stimuli (film clips). The methods describe within-task contrasts (Regulate vs Attend), whole-brain group-level voxelwise analyses with peak coordinates in MNI space (tables and whole-brain results reported), and ROI analyses; participants are healthy adults and results include within-group and between-group effects. These elements satisfy all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis (I5–I11). No exclusion criteria apply.

This fMRI study uses a task (threat vs. safe cues) and reports ROI-based analyses of percent signal change during handholding conditions; however it does not meet critical inclusion criteria for this meta-analysis. Exclusion criteria met: E4 (the report uses an ROI-based approach and extracts parameter estimates from predefined ROIs rather than presenting a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise activation map with peak coordinates). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli: threat/safety cues were presented visually), I8 (eligible sample), I9 (within-task contrast reported: threat > safe). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no instructed emotion-regulation strategy such as cognitive reappraisal or other instructed regulation—regulation here is social/supportive handholding, not an instructed cognitive/regulation task), I10 (no clearly reported whole-brain group voxelwise task-activation maps with peak coordinates). Full text appears complete.

While this is a task-based fMRI study using visual emotional stimuli (I5, I7) with an eligible sample (BD patients and healthy controls; I8), reporting valence contrasts (Negative > Neutral) and providing group-level coordinates/figures (I9, I10, I11), it does NOT instruct participants to regulate their emotional responses. The paradigm presents affective images as irrelevant background distractors during a cognitive interference task (MSIT), but there is no instructed emotion regulation strategy (e.g., reappraise, down-regulate, accept) or regulation cue period. Therefore inclusion criterion I6 (instructed emotion regulation) is not met, and the study must be excluded. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) are triggered. Full text appears complete.

The study is a task-based fMRI investigation using visual emotional stimuli (IAPS and photos) and reports within-task contrasts for unregulated viewing (negative vs neutral) with whole-brain group analyses and peak coordinates. However, participants were not instructed to use any emotion-regulation strategy (e.g., reappraisal, distancing, acceptance); they simply viewed and rated pictures. Therefore the study does not meet the inclusion criterion requiring an instructed emotion-regulation task (I6). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) are triggered by the manuscript. Inclusion criteria met: I5, I7, I8, I9, I10, I11. Inclusion criteria not met: I6. Exclusion criteria applied: []. Full text appears complete (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

This is a task-based fMRI study (I5) using visual emotional stimuli (static faces) (I7) in an eligible sample (children/adolescents; clinical high-risk group with healthy controls reported separately) (I8). The paper reports within-task unregulated viewing contrasts (face > shape) (I9) and presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses normalized to Talairach space with cluster-level results (I10, I11). Although no explicit emotion-regulation instruction was given (I6 not applicable), the meta-analysis objective explicitly allows studies that involve unregulated viewing of visual emotional stimuli, and the study therefore meets the required criteria for inclusion. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This study is a resting-state fMRI seed-based functional connectivity study in bipolar disorder, not a task-based emotion regulation experiment. Exclusion criteria met: E5 (reports only resting-state/seed-based connectivity without any whole-brain task-evoked activation map). Inclusion criteria met: I8 (sample qualifies: clinical and control groups reported). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I5 (not task-based fMRI), I6 (no instructed emotion regulation/cognitive reappraisal task), I7 (no visual emotional stimuli; resting state), I9 (no within-task regulation or viewing contrasts reported), I10 (no whole-brain task-evoked group-level activation maps). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study using visual emotional stimuli (I5, I7). The sample is eligible (healthy adult participants; I8). The paper reports unregulated viewing contrasts (Disgust > Neutral, Fear > Neutral), fulfilling I9. Group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported with thresholds and coordinates (random-effects analyses, ROI and exploratory whole-brain results), meeting I10 and I11. The study did not instruct an explicit emotion-regulation strategy (I6 not met), but the meta-analysis objective permits inclusion of studies that simply view stimuli without regulating; thus lack of an instructed regulation condition does not preclude inclusion. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study is a task-based fMRI with visual emotional face distracters and reports within-task emotion contrasts and whole-brain exploratory results (in supplements), but it does NOT instruct participants to use an explicit emotion-regulation strategy (e.g., reappraisal, distancing). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli — faces), I8 (sample includes youth), I9 (reports within-task emotion-related contrasts: fear vs neutral effects), I10 (references whole-brain results/tables in supplement), I11 (coordinates/tables acceptable in supplement). Inclusion criterion not met: I6 (no instructed emotion-regulation strategy — the task required performing an n-back with emotional distracters rather than an instructed reappraisal or other explicit regulation). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) are triggered. Therefore, per instructions requiring ALL inclusion criteria to be satisfied, I exclude this study because I6 is not met. Full text appears complete.

This task-based fMRI study (faces task) contrasts emotion labeling (an incidental/instructed form of emotion regulation) with emotion matching/gender labeling and reports within-task contrasts (e.g., emotion labeling vs emotion matching) and whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses with thresholded Z-statistic images and peak coordinates. Stimuli are visual (faces). Sample includes adolescents and a control group reported separately. Thus it meets all relevant inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis and violates none of the exclusion criteria.

This is a task-based fMRI study using visual (movie) stimuli in children and adults and reports neural differences for unregulated viewing of positive/negative/neutral clips. However, it does not include any instructed emotion regulation task/strategy (violates I6). The paper reports multivariate classification results and region lists but does not provide a conventional group-level whole-brain task activation contrast with peak coordinates in standard space suitable for coordinate-based meta-analysis (violates I10 and thus I11). Therefore it fails to meet all required inclusion criteria. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli - film clips), I8 (sample qualifies), I9 (reports unregulated viewing condition effects via within-task condition analyses). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no instructed regulation), I10 (no clearly reported whole-brain voxelwise peak coordinates/contrast maps), I11 (no qualifying coordinate tables/figures apparent). No exclusion criteria from the list apply.

This study is a resting-state fMRI investigation of network connectivity in mTBI patients; it does not involve a task-based emotion regulation paradigm or instructed regulation of emotional responses to visual stimuli. Inclusion criteria met: I8 (sample: clinical participants reported separately). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I5 (not task-based fMRI), I6 (no instructed emotion regulation strategy), I7 (no visual emotional stimuli; resting-state only), I9 (no within-task emotion-regulation or unregulated viewing contrasts), I10 (no whole-brain task-evoked activation maps reported). Exclusion criteria met: E5 (reports only resting-state analyses without any task activation maps). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study does not address the review objective and must be excluded.

This is a task-based fMRI study with visual stimuli, whole-brain group-level analyses, and within-task contrasts reported. However, participants were not instructed to use any emotion-regulation strategy; they passively viewed facial primes and pictures and rated arousal. Inclusion criterion I6 (an instructed emotion-regulation strategy) is not met. No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

The study is a task-based fMRI investigation with visual stimuli (I5, I7), includes an appropriate sample (I8), and reports an unregulated within-task contrast (negative > positive) relevant to emotion processing (I9). However, it does not instruct an emotion-regulation strategy during the fMRI task (I6 not met), and the provided full text does not report peak coordinates from a group-level whole-brain statistical map in standard stereotactic space (I10 not met). Although whole-brain analyses are described and supplementary images are referenced, peak coordinates are not present in the supplied content; therefore not all inclusion criteria are satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) are triggered based on the provided text. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study is EXCLUDED because it does not meet inclusion criterion I6: the fMRI task did not instruct an explicit emotion regulation strategy (e.g., reappraisal, acceptance, instructed cognitive control). Instead it probes automatic regulation of emotional conflict (iI–cI) without instruction. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli—faces), I8 (sample includes eligible ages), I9 (reports within-task contrasts indexing emotion conflict and conflict regulation), I10 (reports whole-brain voxelwise analyses with coordinates), and I11 (coordinates/results described and in supplementary material). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Because the review requires instructed/regulation tasks (I6), this automatic/uninstructed regulation paradigm does not qualify for inclusion.

The study is excluded because it does NOT meet I6: the fMRI task is affect labeling, an incidental/implicit process, not an instructed emotion regulation strategy (e.g., reappraisal, distancing, acceptance). Although labeling reduces amygdala activity and is discussed as incidental regulation, participants were not instructed to regulate their emotional responses. Satisfied inclusion criteria: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli: faces), I8 (sample acceptable), I9 (within-task contrasts reported), I10 (group whole-brain maps with coordinates), I11 (results clearly described). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) are met. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empathy (intentional perspective-taking) fMRI study with visual face stimuli and whole-brain analyses. However, participants were instructed to empathize (share emotions), not to apply an emotion regulation strategy (no instructed reappraisal, distancing, acceptance, or other regulation), and the reported emotional contrasts reflect empathy versus baseline rather than an instructed regulation versus baseline/look contrast. This fits exclusion criterion E7 (empathy/perspective-taking with no instruction to amplify or dampen one's own emotional response). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli), I8 (sample acceptable), I10 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses), I11 (whole-brain results reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no instructed emotion-regulation strategy), I9 (no within-task emotion-regulation contrast or a pure unregulated ‘view’ contrast distinct from an empathy instruction). Therefore the study should be excluded.

Full text is complete. This is a task-based fMRI study (I5) that instructed an emotion regulation strategy (attentional deployment) during anticipation (I6), includes an eligible sample (I8), reports within-task regulation contrasts (I9), and provides group-level whole-brain analyses/peak coordinates (I10,I11). However, the emotional stimuli regulated/viewed are auditory (aversive/pleasant sounds) and monetary outcomes rather than visual stimuli; thus it fails Inclusion Criterion I7 (stimuli must be VISUAL). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) are triggered. Therefore the study is excluded because it does not meet I7 (stimulus modality).

This is a task-based fMRI study of frustration in children that includes whole-brain results, but it does not instruct participants to use an emotion-regulation strategy (e.g., reappraisal, distancing) or include an explicit regulation instruction. Therefore it fails the required criterion I6. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study using visual emotional stimuli (IAPS images) and reports unregulated viewing contrasts (emotional valence > neutral) as well as whole-brain voxelwise group analyses with MNI coordinates. Sample includes patient and control groups reported separately. Although no explicit emotion-regulation instruction was given (i.e., I6 ‘instructed regulation’ is not present), the meta-analysis objective accepts studies that involve passive/unregulated viewing; the study therefore satisfies the required within-task unregulated contrast (I9). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Thus the study meets inclusion criteria I5, I7, I8, I9, I10, and I11 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

The study is a task-based fMRI investigation of instructed emotion regulation (engagement vs. distraction) with whole-brain group analyses and within-task contrasts, but the emotional stimuli are auditory (audiotaped stories) rather than visual images or videos. This violates inclusion criterion I7 (stimuli must be VISUAL). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study must be excluded on the basis of not meeting I7.

Excluded because the fMRI task did not instruct an emotion regulation strategy (instructed regulation criterion I6 not met) and the reported fMRI results are reported using small-volume correction/ROI analyses (amygdala SVC) with no accompanying whole-brain, voxelwise group-level task activation map reported, thus violating exclusion criterion E4. The study does meet several inclusion criteria: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual emotional stimuli — faces), I8 (sample acceptable), I9 (reports within-task unregulated viewing contrasts, e.g., faces > baseline), and I11 (coordinates/results reported in text). However it fails I6 (no instructed regulation) and I10 (no whole-brain voxelwise group map). Full text appears complete. Therefore excluded.

This is a task-based fMRI study using visual emotional stimuli (angry and neutral faces) and reports an unregulated viewing contrast (Angry > Neutral) at the group level with whole-brain voxelwise analyses and MNI peak coordinates. Sample is healthy adult participants. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Although no emotion-regulation instruction was given (I6 not met), the meta-analysis accepts unregulated viewing contrasts (I9), so the study addresses the review objective and meets the necessary inclusion criteria.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructed participants to use cognitive distraction (0-back vs 2-back) during anticipation of negative vs neutral IAPS pictures, qualifying as an instructed antecedent-focused emotion-regulation strategy (attentional deployment/cognitive control). Stimuli were visual (IAPS images). The paper reports within-task contrasts addressing regulation effects (e.g. interaction of valence and cognitive load; negative (0-back>2-back) > neutral (0-back>2-back)) and behavioral correlations, all from group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses with peak coordinates in standard space (MNI), satisfying whole-brain reporting. Sample (healthy adult females) is acceptable. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and is suitable for the meta-analysis.

Although this is an empirical task-based fMRI study using visual emotional face stimuli in a healthy adult sample and reports group-level whole-brain results with peak coordinates, it does NOT instruct participants to use an emotion regulation strategy (e.g. reappraisal, distancing, acceptance) and therefore fails inclusion criterion I6. The reported within-task contrasts (affect-incongruent > congruent in an approach–avoidance task) index voluntary control of action tendencies rather than an instructed emotion-regulation manipulation; thus it does not meet I9 (within-task contrast specifically related to instructed emotion regulation or an unregulated viewing contrast). Full text appears complete. Inclusion IDs met: I5, I7, I8, I10, I11. Inclusion IDs not met: I6, I9. No exclusion criteria from the list apply.

The study is a task-based fMRI experiment using visual emotional stimuli (faces) and reports within-task contrasts for unregulated viewing (e.g., emotion > shape) with whole-brain group analyses and reported coordinates. However, it does not instruct participants to apply an explicit emotion regulation strategy (e.g., reappraisal, acceptance, distancing) — tasks are matching and Stroop paradigms requiring cognitive control but not an instructed emotion-regulation strategy.
