Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I6. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) are met. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study using visual stimuli (movie clips and proposal screens) in an Ultimatum Game. The paper reports within-task unregulated viewing contrasts (e.g., unfair > fair) and decision contrasts, with group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses and reported peak activations (tables/figures). The sample (healthy young adult women) is acceptable. Although the study does not instruct an explicit emotion-regulation strategy (e.g., reappraisal), the review objective includes studies that involve unregulated viewing; thus the study meets the review’s criteria for inclusion.

This is a task-based fMRI study (I5) using visual stimuli (video clips; I7) with an eligible sample (I8). The paper reports within-task contrasts (separation vs play; unregulated viewing contrast) and whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses with reported peak clusters (I9, I10, I11). However, the fMRI task did not instruct participants to use an emotion-regulation strategy (no reappraisal/acceptance/distancing instructions); participants simply viewed own and unfamiliar child play and separation scenes. Therefore inclusion criterion I6 (instructed emotion regulation) is not met, and per the requirement that all inclusion criteria be satisfied this study must be excluded. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) are triggered. Full text appears complete.

Full text is complete. The study is a task-based fMRI study of the Ultimatum Game with visual stimuli (faces) and reports whole-brain unfair>fair contrasts. However, it does not instruct participants to use any emotion-regulation strategy (e.g., reappraisal, distancing, acceptance); participants simply decide to accept or reject offers. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I6 (regulated emotion strategy instructed). It meets I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli), I8 (sample acceptable), I9 (within-task contrast unfair>fair reported), I10 (whole-brain analyses reported), and I11 (results presented in text/tables). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply. Conclusion: EXCLUDE because I6 is not met.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs participants to label affect (an instructed strategy shown to function as incidental emotion regulation), using visual stimuli (photographs of faces). The sample includes GAD patients and healthy controls with group-level analyses. The paper reports within-task contrasts (emotion vs. fixation; affect vs. gender) and longitudinal regulation-related contrasts (pre–post changes, group-by-time interactions) and provides whole-brain analyses with peak coordinates in MNI space. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not a review, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-task effects, not an empathy/perspective-taking-only paradigm). Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10, and I11.

Excluded based on E5: the paper reports task-modulated seed-based connectivity (gPPI) results and prediction analyses but does not report any whole-brain, group-level task-evoked activation maps (univariate activation contrasts) with peak coordinates in standard space. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (explicit emotion regulation instruction — positive upregulation), I7 (visual stimuli: IAPS and neutral images), I8 (clinical sample with controls reported separately), I9 (within-task contrast used: Positive Increase > Positive View). Inclusion criterion not met: I10 (no whole-brain task-evoked statistical map reported). Because E5 (reports ONLY seed-based connectivity without also reporting a whole-brain task activation map) is met, the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study using an instructed emotion regulation paradigm (enhance/suppress/attend) employing cognitive reappraisal strategies with visual IAPS images. It reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (e.g., enhance conditions, sustained 2nd half vs 1st half) and voxelwise, whole-brain group-level analyses with peak coordinates in standard space (MNI). The sample includes depressed patients and healthy controls reported separately. No exclusion criteria apply (not a review, includes whole-brain maps, includes within-group task effects, and is not an empathy/perspective-only task). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; supplementary materials are noted but not required. Therefore, all inclusion criteria I5–I11 are satisfied and the study should be INCLUDED.

This study is excluded because it does not test instructed emotion regulation of visual emotional stimuli. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I8 (sample acceptable), I10 (whole-brain group-level analyses reported), I11 (whole-brain results described in text/supplement). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I6 (no instructed emotion regulation strategy; task is a non-emotional Parametric Go/No-Go), I7 (stimuli are non-emotional letters, not visual emotional images/clips), I9 (no within-task contrast related to emotion regulation or unregulated emotional viewing; contrasts are cognitive control: Rejections, Commissions, Targets). No exclusion criteria from the review were triggered. Full text appears complete.

(a) Exclusion criteria met: none.
(b) Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli: on-screen 'safe' vs 'shock' cues), I8 (eligible sample: clinical and control groups), I9 (reports within-task unregulated contrast: shock > safe and shock-I/II contrasts), I10 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with coordinates), I11 (results reported in text/tables).
(c) Inclusion criteria NOT met: I6 (no instruction to participants to regulate or reappraise their emotional responses; the paradigm measured natural anticipatory fear without an instructed emotion-regulation strategy). Therefore the study does not satisfy all required inclusion criteria for the regulation studies; it is excluded. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study using visual stimuli and reports unregulated viewing contrasts and whole-brain results; however the fMRI task did NOT instruct participants to use an emotion regulation strategy (no reappraisal, distancing, or other instructed regulation). The task involved passive viewing of faces and bodies with occasional attractiveness ratings, not instructed regulation. Therefore inclusion criterion I6 is not satisfied. Met inclusion criteria: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli), I8 (sample qualifies), I9 (reports unregulated viewing contrasts: Faces > Scrambled, Bodies > Scrambled), I10 (whole-brain group-level analyses with coordinates), I11 (results clearly described). No exclusion criteria apply (E3–E7: none met). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Exclusion is based on missing I6 (instruction to regulate).

This is a task-based whole-brain fMRI study (I5 and I10 satisfied) but does not meet key inclusion criteria for the review: (I6) participants were not instructed to use any emotion-regulation strategy — regulation was spontaneous/implicit rather than instructed; (I7) the emotional stimuli are interpersonal social interactions (Ultimatum Game offers and verbal negotiations), not standardized visual emotional stimuli (e.g., IAPS pictures, affective faces/scenes, or film clips); (I9) the analyses do not report within-task contrasts of instructed regulation (e.g., reappraise > look) or unregulated viewing contrasts of visual stimuli as defined by the review. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) are triggered by the manuscript. Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false). Hence excluded for failing to meet I6, I7, and I9 while satisfying I5 and I10.

Although this is a task-based fMRI study with appropriate within-task contrasts (SC>NT, SP>NT) and whole-brain, group-level analyses reported (satisfying I5, I9, I10, and I11), it does not meet critical inclusion criteria for this meta-analysis. The experiment did not instruct participants to use an emotion-regulation strategy (no reappraisal, acceptance, distancing, or other regulated instructions)—participants were asked to focus on the meaning and any emotional responses, not to regulate them (I6 not met). Crucially, the emotional stimuli are words/adjectives presented visually; the review’s stimulus inclusion specifically excludes word/sentence stimulus studies (I7 not met). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) are triggered. Therefore the study must be excluded.

This is a task-based fMRI study using visual emotional stimuli (fearful faces) with both implicit (passive/gender) and explicit (emotion labeling) conditions, and reports within-task emotion contrasts (e.g., fear > neutral) and whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses. Participant groups include alcohol-dependent patients and controls with results reported across groups. Full methods, results, and discussion are present. Although no instructed emotion-regulation strategy (e.g., reappraisal) was given, the review objective allows inclusion of unregulated viewing contrasts; such contrasts and their whole-brain results are reported. Therefore the study meets the review’s requirements for inclusion as an unregulated viewing fMRI study of visual emotional stimuli.

This study is a task-based fMRI investigation of affective anticipation using visual stimuli and reports whole-brain voxelwise contrasts, but it does NOT instruct participants to use an emotion regulation strategy (e.g., reappraisal, distancing, acceptance). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli), I8 (sample acceptable), I9 (within-task contrast: unpleasant > pleasant anticipation), I10 (whole-brain voxelwise maps), I11 (results reported via brain maps/tables). Inclusion criterion not met: I6 (no instructed emotion regulation). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply. Full text appears complete.

This study is a task-based fMRI comparison of adolescents and adults viewing emotional face stimuli under 'directed' (explicit emotion judgment) and 'incidental' (age judgment) conditions. It meets inclusion criteria I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli—faces), I8 (sample: healthy adolescents and adults), I9 (reports within-task contrasts including incidental vs fixation and directed vs fixation—i.e. unregulated viewing contrasts), I10 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with coordinates), and I11 (results reported with coordinates/tables). However, it does NOT meet I6: no instructed emotion regulation strategy (e.g., reappraisal, distancing, acceptance) was required—the tasks manipulate attention to emotion but do not instruct participants to regulate their emotions. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply. Therefore the study is excluded because it fails to satisfy inclusion criterion I6 (instruction to regulate an emotional response).

This study is a task-based fMRI investigation (I5) of older adults (sample acceptable, I8) and reports an unregulated emotional-versus-neutral contrast (eStroop emotional > neutral), satisfying I9. However, it does NOT instruct participants to regulate their emotional responses (no reappraisal/other instructed regulation)—so I6 is not met. Critically, the emotional stimuli are words (emotional/neutral words) rather than pictorial/visual images or film; the inclusion criteria explicitly exclude studies whose regulated/viewed stimuli are word or sentence stimuli, so I7 is not met. Because ALL inclusion criteria must be satisfied and I6 and I7 are not satisfied, the study must be excluded. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) are triggered by the information provided. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion).

This is a task-based, whole-brain fMRI study using visual emotional stimuli (IAPS) in healthy volunteers and reports within-task contrasts (negative > neutral/target) and whole-brain voxelwise results. However, the task did not instruct an emotion regulation strategy (participants performed an emotional oddball target-detection task and merely viewed distractor pictures), so inclusion criterion I6 (instructed emotion regulation) is not satisfied. Summary: Inclusion criteria met: I5, I7, I8, I9, I10, I11. Inclusion criteria not met: I6. Exclusion criteria met: none (E3–E7 not applicable). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Because ALL inclusion criteria must be satisfied and I6 is not met, the study is excluded.

Full text indicates an empirical task-based fMRI study but uses emotional word stimuli in an emotional Go/NoGo task without any instructed emotion-regulation strategy. Exclusion rationale: (a) Exclusion IDs met: none of the explicit exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply. (b) Inclusion IDs met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I8 (sample includes clinical and control groups), I9 (reports within-task emotional contrasts such as Negative > Neutral), I10 (group-level whole-brain/voxelwise results with peak coordinates in MNI space), I11 (results reported in tables/figures/text). (c) Inclusion IDs NOT met: I7 (stimuli are word/sentence stimuli, which the protocol excludes), and I6 (no instructed emotion-regulation strategy — task probes emotional processing and inhibition rather than reappraisal/explicit regulation). Because I7 is explicitly exclusionary and I6 is not satisfied, the study does not meet all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis and must be excluded.

This study is excluded because it does not instruct an emotion-regulation strategy (inclusion criterion I6 not met). It is a task-based fMRI study (I5 met) using visual emotional stimuli (I7 met: IAPS and facial images) with an eligible sample including schizophrenia patients and controls (I8 met). The analysis reports within-task contrasts of emotional viewing (fearful > neutral) for groups (I9 met) and describes group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses in SPM (I10 met) with results clearly described in the text (I11 met). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) are triggered. Therefore the single required inclusion criterion I6 (instructed emotion regulation) is not satisfied, so the paper must be excluded.

Full text appears complete. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI: participants were scanned while viewing IAPS pictures), I7 (visual stimuli: IAPS static images), I9 (reports within-task unregulated viewing contrasts: unpleasant>neutral and unpleasant>pleasant), I10 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analysis with cluster correction) and I11 (results/coordinates clearly described). Inclusion criterion not met: I6 (no instructed emotion regulation strategy — participants passively viewed and rated valence; no reappraisal/acceptance/distancing or other regulation instructions were given). No exclusion criteria from the list apply (e.g., study is empirical, reports whole-brain activation, not only ROI/connectivity, and includes within-task contrasts). Because at least one required inclusion criterion (I6) is not satisfied, the study must be excluded for this review.

This is a task-based fMRI study using visual emotional stimuli (static sad and fearful faces) with an implicit viewing task (gender judgment). It reports within-task unregulated viewing contrasts (Fear > Neutral, Sad > Neutral) and whole-brain, group-level analyses with reported peak coordinates and cluster results; patient and control groups are reported separately. Thus it satisfies I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli), I8 (sample includes clinical patients with controls reported), I9 (reports unregulated viewing contrasts), I10 (group-level whole-brain task activation maps), and I11 (results reported in text/figures). The study did not instruct an emotion-regulation strategy (I6 not met), but the review objective accepts unregulated viewing contrasts per I9. No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only or connectivity-only reporting). Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study that uses visual stimuli (video clips) and reports whole-brain, group-level task activation results; however, participants passively viewed emotion-eliciting videos (sad, gambling, cocaine) with no instruction to use an emotion-regulation strategy (e.g., reappraisal, distancing) and no regulation instruction is described. Therefore the study fails inclusion criterion I6 (regulated-emotion instruction). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli — videos), I8 (eligible sample with groups reported), I9 (reports within-task unregulated viewing contrasts / emotion>baseline and condition contrasts), I10 (whole-brain voxelwise analyses), I11 (results clearly described). No exclusion criteria are met. Because at least one required inclusion criterion (I6) is not satisfied, the study is excluded.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs participants to regulate emotional responses (increase positive, decrease negative) to visual IAPS pictures. The paper reports within-task contrasts (increase > watch; decrease > watch), whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses in MNI space with coordinates and appropriate multiple-comparison correction, and includes complete methods, results, and discussion. Sample and stimuli meet the review’s eligibility. No exclusion criteria are met.

Full text is complete. This is a task-based fMRI study (I5) with adolescent participants (I8). It reports unregulated viewing contrasts (e.g., SWE>NEU), satisfying I9, and provides group-level whole-brain voxelwise results with coordinates and cluster correction, satisfying I10 and I11. However, the fMRI task did NOT instruct an emotion regulation strategy (no reappraisal/acceptance/distancing instructions), so it fails I6. Critically, the emotional stimuli are written words (swear/negative/positive/neutral words); the review’s inclusion rule excludes studies whose regulated stimuli are word/sentence stimuli, so it fails I7. Because NOT ALL required inclusion criteria are met (I6 and I7 are not satisfied), the study must be excluded. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) are triggered by this paper.

This is a task-based (Cyberball) fMRI study that uses visual stimuli and reports whole-brain, voxelwise contrasts (Exclusion vs Inclusion, Inclusion vs Rest) with stereotactic peak coordinates; sample includes clinical group and controls. However, participants were not instructed to use any emotion-regulation strategy (no reappraisal, distancing, acceptance, or instructed cognitive control); the task elicits an unregulated emotional response to social exclusion rather than an instructed regulation condition. Per the review’s requirement to satisfy all inclusion criteria, I6 (instruction of an emotion-regulation strategy) is not met. Thus the study must be excluded. Full text appears complete.

The full text describes a task-based fMRI study (n=18) that instructs attentional deployment (focus-on-gains vs focus-on-missed-chances) as an emotion-regulation manipulation during presentation of visual outcome stimuli. Behavioral and neural contrasts directly test regulation (GF vs MF; e.g., GF>MF) and unregulated viewing contrasts (Opt>Nopt). Whole-brain group-level analyses are reported with MNI peak coordinates and FWE correction. All required elements are present (task fMRI, instructed regulation strategy, visual stimuli, suitable sample, within-task regulation contrasts, whole-brain reporting). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Full text review: This is a task-based fMRI study using visual stimuli (video clips) of participants' own vs unfamiliar children, with whole-brain, voxelwise analyses and coordinate tables reported. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli—video clips), I8 (sample qualifies—clinical mothers), I9 (reports within-task unregulated viewing contrasts: Own Positive>Stranger Positive, Own Negative>Stranger Negative), I10 (whole-brain group-level voxelwise analyses), I11 (coordinates reported in tables). Inclusion criterion not met: I6 (no instructed emotion regulation strategy; participants passively viewed clips with no instruction to reappraise, distance, accept, or otherwise regulate). Exclusion criteria: none met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, contains within-task effects). Because the protocol requires all inclusion criteria to be satisfied and this study lacks an instructed emotion-regulation condition (I6), it must be excluded from analyses restricted to instructed regulation paradigms. Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using visual emotional stimuli (IAPS images) and an instructed regulation task (Think/No-Think retrieval suppression) that aims to modulate affect. The methods report within-task contrasts (e.g., No-Think > Think; Intrusion vs Non-Intrusion) and relate neural activity to affective outcomes. Group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported with MNI coordinates and FWE correction. The sample comprises healthy adult participants. Thus all inclusion criteria are met, and no exclusion criteria apply. Although the instructed strategy is memory retrieval suppression rather than classical reappraisal, criterion I6 explicitly allows instructed cognitive control of an emotional response, which this task implements. Full text appears complete (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).
